mem.t: Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.

lessons.title: The Principle of the Grain of Wheat
lessons.theme: Life multiplies when we willingly fall into the ground and die

v: Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
He who loves his life will lose it. He who hates his life in this world will keep it to eternal life.

lessons.still: Cup your hands together as if holding a single seed; then slowly open them and turn your palms downward. Say to the Lord, “Lord, I place myself in your hands. I am willing to fall into whatever soil you choose for me.” Be still for one minute — asking not for results, only for obedience.
teach: A grain of wheat kept in a beautiful box can last for years, yet it will only ever be one grain. Bury it in the soil and it seems to disappear — but the next year it rises as a stalk heavy with grain. Spiritual multiplication works the same way: when we preserve ourselves, life stops with us; when we give ourselves away, life multiplies.

Jesus spoke these words just as some Greeks had come asking to see him. The door to the nations was about to open, yet he talked about dying. He knew that the way to life for all people had to pass through the cross. Verse 25 extends the same principle to his disciples: to “love” one's life is to cling tightly to oneself; to “hate” it is to stop letting oneself be the centre.

This week we enter the fourth stage: Multiplying. Many people think multiplication is a matter of methods and techniques, but first of all it is a death — dying to “my reputation, my time, my comfort.” When our mindset turns from “I want to be blessed” to “I want to become a seed,” our life begins to bear much fruit.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The grain of the self-ruled life cannot bear to fall to the ground, and so it forever “remains by itself alone”; the grain of the self-emptied life is willing to die, and so it enters into the limitless and lives out the limitless. Multiplication is not doing more ministry; it is letting the life of Jesus flow to more people through my “death,” with all the glory going to him.
q: Who is God? — The Lord himself first became the grain of wheat that fell to the ground. What kind of love does that show you?
Who am I? — What part of your life is still “kept in a box,” something you cannot bear to hand over?
How shall I respond? — In what small matter today are you willing to “fall into the ground”?
lessons.jesus: Jesus did not merely teach this principle; he became that grain of wheat himself. He was buried in a tomb and rose on the third day. On the day of Pentecost three thousand people turned to the Lord in a single day, and to this very day he is bearing fruit among every nation and people. Our own faith today is fruit from that one grain.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for willingly becoming the grain of wheat that fell into the ground, so that I might have life. I confess that I often love myself and protect myself. Help me to be willing to fall to the ground and die to my self-centredness, so that your life may bear much fruit through me. Glory to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down one thing you “cannot bear to give up,” and pray it over into the Lord's hands
Today, set aside your own convenience once in order to help someone else
Memorise John 12:24 and repeat it silently three times
lessons.noon: “Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone.” — Lord, right now I am willing to fall into your hands.

lessons.title: The Great Commission
lessons.theme: The Lord's command is to make disciples, not just to win decisions

v: Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.

lessons.still: Imagine yourself standing on the mountain in Galilee with the risen Lord right in front of you. Quietly hear him say, “Go.” Take a deep breath, and one by one place the places you will go today — home, work, church — under his authority.
teach: If a factory only produced parts and never assembled them, it could never build a single car, however full its warehouse. If a church only chases raised hands and decisions, but no one walks alongside those people as they grow into disciples, it is just a warehouse full of parts. The Lord's Great Commission is not “win decisions” but “make disciples of all nations.”

The heart of this passage is “make disciples,” accompanied by three actions: “go,” “baptize,” and “teach them to observe.” Notice the word is “observe,” not merely “know.” A disciple is not someone who has heard many sermons but someone who lives out the Lord's word. Before the command stands the foundation of authority — “All authority has been given to me” — and after it the promise of presence — “I am with you always.”

The Great Commission is not a professional assignment for a handful of ministers; it is the life mission of every disciple. Here is the mindset change: I am not part of the church's “audience”; I am a sent “disciple-maker.” We do not have to rely on our own eloquence or ability, because the One who sends us holds all authority in heaven and on earth.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The Great Commission is the very blueprint for building what belongs to God — disciples generation after generation, so that God's kingdom comes on earth. We go by the Lord's authority, not our own; we teach people to obey the Lord's word, not to follow us. Letting Jesus reign begins with obeying this command.
q: Who is God? — What kind of security do “all authority” and “I am with you always” give you?
Who am I? — Are you more like an audience member of the Great Commission, or a disciple who has been sent?
How shall I respond? — Who in your life is the Lord asking you to “go” and walk alongside for a while?
lessons.jesus: This is exactly how Jesus made disciples. In just over three years he wrote no books and built no buildings; instead he ate, lived and walked with twelve men, teaching them and sending them out. Before he ascended he entrusted the mission to them; they passed it on to the next generation, until it reached our hands.
lessons.pray: Risen Lord, thank you for entrusting the Great Commission to ordinary people like me. I confess that I often just want to be a spectator. Send me, by your authority and with your presence, to walk with one person as they come to know you and obey your word. May your kingdom come. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the names of three people around you who do not yet know the Lord or are new believers
Pray for one of them, asking the Lord to open the way for you to walk with them for a season
Today, share in one sentence with a brother or sister something you have learned from the Lord's word
lessons.noon: “Go and make disciples of all nations.” — Lord, send me right now to love one person.

lessons.title: Life Passing On Life
lessons.theme: The gospel is passed on through lives, not only through words

v: But we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother cherishes her own children.
Even so, affectionately longing for you, we were well pleased to impart to you not the Good News of God only, but also our own souls, because you had become very dear to us.
that which we have seen and heard we declare to you, that you also may have fellowship with us. Yes, and our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son, Jesus Christ.

lessons.still: Think back to someone whose life shaped your faith — perhaps a parent, an older believer, or a small-group leader. Speak their name before the Lord and give thanks for them. Then quietly ask, “Lord, whose life could I be that person for?”
teach: One torch can light another without losing any of its own light; but an unlit torch, however finely made, cannot light anything. Passing on spiritual life is like that: we can only pass on the life we truly have within us.

Looking back on his ministry in Thessalonica, Paul uses the picture of a mother: “gentle among you, like a nursing mother cherishes her own children.” He was willing to share not only the gospel but “our own souls” as well. John likewise says that what he declares is “that which we have seen and heard,” so “that you also may have fellowship with us.” The gospel is not a handout; it is a life that can be seen.

So multiplication is not first of all learning a method; it is giving people the chance to see up close the life of Christ in me. Here is the mindset change: people do not follow my perfection, but how I lean on the Lord in weakness and return to him after failure. Authenticity passes on life far better than perfection.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Life passes on life — the life of Christ first dwells in me, then flows to others through relationships. This is 920 extended: living out the “0” of the self-emptied life toward my “2,” bearing the “9,” the fruit of the Spirit — and the seeds inside that fruit can bring forth new life.
q: Who is God? — What wisdom does God show in passing the gospel to you through people?
Who am I? — When others look at you, do they see a handout or a life?
How shall I respond? — Whom are you willing to let see your life of faith more closely?
lessons.jesus: Jesus chose his disciples so that “they might be with him.” Peter saw the Lord walk on the water and experienced the Lord washing his feet; John leaned against the Lord's chest. What they later passed on was not theory but lives transformed by the life of Jesus.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for passing your life on to me through people who love you. Make me not merely a messenger of words but a carrier of life. Let others see your grace in my honesty, and make me willing to give them my heart and my time. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write a word of thanks and send it to someone who has shaped your faith
Invite a brother or sister for a meal and share your lives with each other
Today, honestly say in front of someone, “I need the Lord”
lessons.noon: “We were well pleased to impart to you not the Good News of God only, but also our own souls” — Lord, right now make me willing to give myself.

lessons.title: Life First, Then Relationships, Then Ministry
lessons.theme: When the order is right, multiplication can last

v: He appointed twelve, that they might be with him, and that he might send them out to preach
and to have authority to heal sicknesses and to cast out demons:
I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.

lessons.still: Sit quietly and do nothing — simply be with the Lord for five minutes. If your to-do list starts to surface, gently set it aside and say to the Lord, “Lord, you first, and then these things.”
teach: If you rush to raise the roof and decorate a house without laying a proper foundation, the taller it grows the faster it falls. Serving is the same. Many people throw themselves eagerly into ministry, only to find a few years later that they are dried up and wounded — or have even wounded others. The problem is often not ability but order.

Mark records Jesus appointing the twelve apostles, and the order is clear: first “that they might be with him,” then “that he might send them out to preach,” and then that they might “have authority.” John 15:5 puts it even more directly: only by remaining in the Lord do we bear much fruit — “apart from me you can do nothing.” Life is the root, relationships are the trunk, ministry is the fruit; fruit is not tied on, it grows naturally from the root.

Here is the mindset change: life first, then relationships, then ministry. People matter more than tasks, relationships matter more than things — do not hurt people for the sake of getting things done. Multiplication is not pulling more people into ministry; it is helping more people first connect with God in life, then connect with one another in love, and ministry will grow naturally.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The order of the fivefold change is mindset, life, lifestyle, relationships, ministry. Skipping life and relationships to jump into ministry is living from the head by yourself; starting from time with the Lord is living from the heart by the Spirit. First with God, then with ourselves, then with others, then with tasks — this is the firm foundation of God's kingdom system.
q: Who is God? — The Lord wanted his disciples first to “be with him.” What does that show you about what he values most?
Who am I? — Lately, in trying to get things done well, have you neglected God or hurt people?
How shall I respond? — How will you put “being with the Lord” back in first place today?
lessons.jesus: Even in the busiest seasons of his ministry, Jesus rose before dawn and went to a solitary place to pray (Mark 1:35). His living connection with the Father was the source of all his service; his love for his disciples was the foundation of his relationships; only then came healing, teaching and sending. His ministry was never bigger than his life.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, I confess that I often put ministry ahead of you, and I have hurt people for the sake of getting things done. Forgive me. Help me first to remain in you, and then to connect with others in love. May my service flow naturally from your life, not from my own strength. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before doing any ministry today, spend ten quiet minutes with the Lord first
If you have hurt someone for the sake of a task, take the initiative to apologise to them today
Review this week's schedule and adjust one thing that has been crowding out your devotional time
lessons.noon: “He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit.” — Lord, right now I return to you first.

lessons.title: I Too Can Be a Blessing
lessons.theme: Those who are blessed are called to become a blessing to others

v: I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing.
I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse him who treats you with contempt. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”

lessons.still: Open your hands with palms facing up and receive: “Lord, thank you for blessing me.” Then turn your palms outward as if handing something on: “Lord, make me a blessing to others.” Slowly repeat this three times.
teach: The Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea both receive water from the Jordan River. The Sea of Galilee takes in and also flows out; it teems with fish and life flourishes all around it. The Dead Sea only takes in and never gives out; however much water it receives, it cannot support a single fish. Spiritual life is the same: if we only receive and never pour out, we stagnate; when life flows in and out, it never stops renewing.

When God called Abram, he gave a string of promises beginning “I will”: I will make of you a great nation, I will bless you and make your name great. Then immediately comes a mission: “You will be a blessing,” reaching finally to “all the families of the earth will be blessed through you.” God's blessing is never the end point but a channel; it came to Abram in order to flow on to every nation.

This week we have seen the grain of wheat falling to the ground, the Great Commission, life passing on life, and life first, ministry later. Today, say to yourself, “I can too.” You do not have to wait until you are more spiritual or more gifted; the grace you have already received is enough to bless one person. Next week we begin with the most basic relationship — the “2,” spiritual companions.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-ruled person keeps blessing for himself and becomes a Dead Sea; the self-emptied person lets blessing flow through him and becomes a channel. The 235 relationships are the riverbeds along which blessing flows: walking with spiritual companions, being spiritual parents to spiritual children, serving alongside fellow soldiers. Letting Jesus receive all the glory means not keeping the blessing for ourselves.
q: Who is God? — Why does the God who says “I will bless you” also say “You will be a blessing”?
Who am I? — Is your spiritual life more like the Sea of Galilee or the Dead Sea?
How shall I respond? — Which grace you received this week could flow on to someone else?
lessons.jesus: God's promise to Abraham was finally fulfilled in Jesus: through him the nations are blessed (Galatians 3:14). Everything Jesus received from the Father he gave away — his time, his healing, his teaching, even his life. He is the river of blessing flowing out to all peoples.
lessons.pray: God who blesses, thank you for the countless graces you have given me in Jesus. I do not want to be a Dead Sea that only takes in. Make me a channel through which your love, truth and hope flow to the people around me. Beginning with one person, let others be blessed through me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the grace you received most deeply this week
Share that grace in one sentence with a friend
Pray for the spiritual companion you will begin walking with next week
lessons.noon: “You will be a blessing.” — Lord, right now make me a blessing to one person.

mem.t: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.

lessons.title: David and Jonathan
lessons.theme: Covenant friendship strengthens us to lean on God

v: When he had finished speaking to Saul, the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was on him and gave it to David with his clothing, even including his sword, his bow, and his sash.

lessons.still: Quietly recall a friend who held you up when you were weak, and thank God for them. Then ask the Lord, “Lord, do you want me to be someone's Jonathan?” Let a face slowly come to mind.
teach: Mountain climbers often tie themselves to their teammates with a rope. On level ground the rope seems unnecessary; but the moment someone slips, it becomes a lifeline. A spiritual companion is a rope like that: keeping each other company in ordinary times, and holding each other fast in a crisis.

Jonathan was a prince — humanly speaking, the heir to the throne — while David was the one God had anointed as the next king. Jonathan could have seen David as a threat. Instead he “loved him as his own soul” and gave him his robe, his armour, his sword and his bow, laying down his own status and rights. Later, when David was being hunted, Jonathan went to him in the forest and “strengthened his hand in God” (1 Samuel 23:16).

A spiritual companion is not just a friend you get along with; it is someone who helps you lean more on God. A good companion does not pull you toward himself but pushes you toward God. Here is the mindset change: I need a companion not because I am hopelessly weak, but because God never designed people to walk alone.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Jonathan is the model of a self-emptied friendship — laying down power and returning to his place, so that God's will could be fulfilled in David. The “2” of 235, the spiritual companion, is exactly this kind of relationship: helping each other succeed rather than competing. Pride provokes pride, but humility draws out humility, and both win.
q: Who is God? — God provided Jonathan for David. What does that show you about his care?
Who am I? — In friendship, do you more often think about what you can “gain” or how you can help the other “succeed”?
How shall I respond? — Whom would you like to invite to be your spiritual companion?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus sent out his disciples, he sent them two by two (Luke 10:1). In the Garden of Gethsemane he took Peter, James and John with him and said, “Stay here, and watch with me.” Even the Son of God, in his humanity, treasured the company of companions.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for the people you have placed in my life to hold me up. Give me a spiritual companion like Jonathan, and make me a Jonathan to someone else. Keep me from envy and competition; let me desire only to help the other person lean more on you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: List two or three people who could become spiritual companions, and pray for them
Send a message of encouragement to a friend who is going through a hard time
Arrange to meet or call a brother or sister this week
lessons.noon: “Jonathan loved him as his own soul.” — Lord, right now teach me to love my companion with your love.

lessons.title: Confessing and Praying for One Another
lessons.theme: In fellowship in the light, bearing one another, we are healed

v: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.
Brothers, even if a man is caught in some fault, you who are spiritual must restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, looking to yourself so that you also aren’t tempted.
Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.

lessons.still: Quietly ask the Holy Spirit to shine his light: “Lord, what have I been hiding, too afraid to let anyone know?” Do not rush to deal with it; simply acknowledge that it is there. Then ask the Lord to give you a trustworthy companion to walk with you in the light.
teach: A wound kept bandaged and hidden from the light may look fine on the surface while festering underneath. When a doctor opens and cleans it, it hurts — but that is where healing begins. Sin is like this: the longer it stays hidden in the dark, the more power it has to control us; only when it is brought into the light is healing possible.

James says, “Confess your offenses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed.” Forgiving sin is God's work — when we confess to God we are forgiven — but healing often happens in the company of brothers and sisters. Paul reminds us to restore people “in a spirit of gentleness,” while “looking to yourself,” and to “bear one another's burdens.” This is not judging; it is carrying.

Spiritual companions need a safe space: weaknesses spoken there will not be passed on or looked down on, but held up in prayer. Here is the mindset change: confession is not humiliation but freedom; intercession is not a polite formality but sharing the load. Become a trustworthy person first, and others will dare to open up to you.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-ruled person protects his image and would rather hide than admit wrong; the self-emptied person returns to his place and admits that he is a sinner saved by grace. Humility is the key to revival — when two people are both willing to let go of their pride, they can have fellowship with each other in the light, and the Holy Spirit has room to do his healing work.
q: Who is God? — Why does God want us not only to confess to him but also to “confess to one another”?
Who am I? — Are you someone people feel safe opening up to, or someone they fear will judge them?
How shall I respond? — To which trustworthy companion are you willing to share a struggle that needs prayer?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said to the woman caught in adultery, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more.” He neither made light of sin nor humiliated the person. He prayed for Peter that his faith would not fail (Luke 22:32), and after Peter fell he personally restored him.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often hide my weaknesses, afraid of being seen. Give me courage to walk in the light, and give me a companion with whom I can confess and pray for one another. Make me gentle in restoring others, faithful in keeping their confidences, and willing to carry their burdens. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Share one matter that needs prayer with a trustworthy companion
Pray specifically for a friend's burden, and let them know you are praying for them
Resolve today not to repeat any weakness someone else has shared with you
lessons.noon: “Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed.” — Lord, right now I choose to live in the light.

lessons.title: Iron Sharpens Iron
lessons.theme: A true friend's faithful words sharpen the edge of our life

v: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.

lessons.still: Recall a recent reminder that made you uncomfortable but was right. Quietly admit before the Lord, “Lord, those words stung, but I am willing to be taught.” Lay down your defensiveness, like setting a shield on the ground.
teach: When two blades are rubbed against each other, sparks fly and the sound grates on the ear — but afterwards both blades are sharper. A knife wrapped only in soft cloth will never be scratched, but it will slowly grow dull. Spiritual companions also need a little “friction.”

Proverbs says, “Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend's countenance” — friends shape and spur one another on. Verse 6 is even more direct: “The wounds of a friend are faithful.” A true friend is willing to risk hurting the relationship in order to speak the truth, while an enemy offers “profuse kisses” that look intimate but do no good.

Sharpening needs two conditions: both must be iron, and they must be close. Speaking the truth must come from love, within a relationship of trust; hearing the truth requires a humble heart. Here is the mindset change: being corrected is not being rejected but being built up. Do not look only for friends who make you comfortable; treasure the friends who make you more like Jesus.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Scripture is my standard — iron sharpening iron does not mean grinding the other person down by my own standards, but standing together before God's word to be pruned. The focus is not on the other person's faults but on both of us becoming more like Jesus. The one who speaks must be self-emptied, not out to win; the one who listens must be self-emptied, not out to defend.
q: Who is God? — God trains us through the faithful words of friends. What kind of love does that reveal?
Who am I? — Are you more afraid of “speaking the truth” or of “hearing the truth”?
How shall I respond? — With what attitude will you respond today to a reminder you would rather not hear?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan!” Strong words — but spoken to rescue him from “not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.” The same Lord later gently asked Peter three times, “Do you love me?” His truth always carries a love that restores.
lessons.pray: Lord, remove the pride in me that fears correction, so that I can humbly receive a friend's faithful words. Give me wisdom and love to speak the truth to my companion at the right time and in the right way. Let us sharpen one another and become more and more like you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Ask a companion directly, “Is there anything you see in me lately that needs adjusting?”
When someone corrects you, simply say “Thank you” — without defending yourself
Lovingly speak a word of honest encouragement to a companion
lessons.noon: “Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.” — Lord, right now make me humble and teachable.

lessons.title: Practising Conversation with Companions
lessons.theme: When we talk together around the Lord's word, our hearts burn within us

v: Then those who feared the LORD spoke one with another; and the LORD listened and heard, and a book of memory was written before him for those who feared the LORD and who honored his name.
They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”

lessons.still: Quietly imagine yourself walking on the road to Emmaus with a companion beside you. A stranger draws near and joins your conversation — it is the Lord himself. Say to him, “Lord, walk with us in our conversation.”
teach: When friends meet, they often talk about the weather, work, children and the news, but seldom about what God has been doing in their lives. It is not that they do not want to; they are simply not used to it and do not know where to begin. Like learning a new language, spiritual conversation takes deliberate practice before it feels natural.

In Malachi's day the spiritual climate was low, yet a group of “those who feared Yahweh spoke one with another,” and God “listened, and heard,” and even recorded it in a book of remembrance. On the road to Emmaus two disciples talked as they walked, and Jesus joined them; afterwards they said, “Weren't our hearts burning within us?” When companions talk together about God's word and works, the Lord is there among them.

You can begin with three simple questions: “What has God said to you this week?” “Where have you experienced God?” “What can I pray for you?” Meetings need not be long, but they should be regular, sincere, and end in prayer. Here is the mindset change: a spiritual companionship is not one deep conversation but an ongoing journey together.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The three foundations are put into practice in conversation — talking about Jesus as our example, Scripture as our standard, and the Holy Spirit as our guide. The focus of the conversation is not complaining about others or tallying up our circumstances, but Jesus. Share from the heart; do not debate from the head. When we use the heart, we find joy — and the Lord bends his ear to listen.
q: Who is God? — God “listened, and heard” the conversations of those who feared him. How does that change the way you see everyday conversation?
Who am I? — How much of your conversation with friends is about God?
How shall I respond? — With whom will you have a spiritual conversation this week using the three questions?
lessons.jesus: On the road to Emmaus Jesus first asked, “What are you talking about as you walk?” He listened first, then, beginning from Moses and all the prophets, explained the Scriptures, and finally was recognised in the breaking of bread. Jesus modelled the best kind of spiritual conversation: listening, opening up the truth, and leading people to meet him.
lessons.pray: Lord, may my mouth speak not only of earthly things but often of your works. Walk with me and my companions in our conversations; open our hearts and set them burning. Teach me to listen first, then to share, and finally to pray together. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Arrange a fifteen-minute conversation with a companion using the three questions
In one conversation today, naturally share something God has done
Agree with a companion on a regular time to talk (weekly or fortnightly)
lessons.noon: “Then those who feared the LORD spoke one with another; and the LORD listened and heard” — Lord, right now may my words be heard by you.

lessons.title: Walking with the Self-Emptied
lessons.theme: When two self-emptied people walk together, the Lord is the third strand between them

v: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

lessons.still: Meditate quietly: is the Lord standing in the middle between me and my friends? Bring your one or two closest companions before the Lord one by one, and say, “Lord, be the strand that binds us together.”
teach: Two thin cords twisted together are stronger than one; add a third strand, and the three wound together do not merely add up their strength — they lock each other fast. Many people think of marriage when they read “a threefold cord,” but it also pictures spiritual companions: two people, with the Lord in the middle.

Philippians names both the poison and the antidote in companion relationships. The poison is “rivalry” and “conceit” — wanting to compare, wanting to win. The antidote is “in humility, each counting others better than himself,” “not just looking to his own things, but also to the things of others.” Two self-ruled people together wear each other out; two self-emptied people together build each other up.

This week we learned covenant from Jonathan, confession and prayer from James, iron sharpening iron from Proverbs, and conversation from Emmaus. Today's summary is this: first become a self-emptied companion yourself, then look for self-emptied companions. Next week we move from the side-by-side “2” to the life-passing “3” — becoming spiritual parents.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility draws out humility, and both win; pride provokes pride, and both lose. The “2” of 235 is not mutual dependence but leaning on the Lord together; when Jesus reigns between two people, their friendship becomes the smallest building block of God's kingdom system.
q: Who is God? — The Lord is willing to be the strand in the middle of our friendships. How does that shape the way you see your friendships?
Who am I? — In companionship, do you more often look to your own interests or to the interests of others?
How shall I respond? — How will you concretely “count others better than yourself” this week?
lessons.jesus: When the disciples argued on the road about who was the greatest, Jesus brought a little child and stood him in their midst; at the Last Supper he wrapped a towel around himself and washed their feet. He wanted his disciples' companionship to be not a contest of rank but mutual service. The Lord himself is the self-emptied companion who stands in the middle.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, tear down the comparison and competition in my friendships. Make me humble, counting others better than myself and caring for my companions' needs. Be the strand that binds us together, so that we lean on you with one heart and grow together. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Pray for your spiritual companion, asking the Lord to make them flourish even more than you
Do one thing that serves only the other person's needs, not your own convenience
Share your biggest takeaway of the week with your companion, and set your next conversation
lessons.noon: “And a threefold cord is not quickly broken.” — Lord, right now be here among us.

mem.t: The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same things to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.

lessons.title: Paul and Timothy
lessons.theme: A spiritual father and son, one in heart and labour for the gospel

v: For I have no one else like-minded, who will truly care about you.
For they all seek their own, not the things of Jesus Christ.
But you know that he has proved himself. As a child serves a father, so he served with me in furtherance of the Good News.
having been reminded of the sincere faith that is in you, which lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and, I am persuaded, in you also.

lessons.still: Quietly recall who, on your journey of faith, helped you grow like a father or mother. Speak their name to the Lord and give thanks. If no one comes to mind, say to the Lord, “Lord, you know what I need, and you know what I can give.”
teach: A child learning to swim could watch a hundred instructional videos and still not learn as much as from being held up in the pool by a pair of hands and hearing, “Don't be afraid — I'm right here.” Spiritual growth is the same: it needs a pair of hands to hold us up. That is what spiritual parents are.

Paul met young Timothy in Lystra (Acts 16:1–3) and took him along to travel and to suffer together. Timothy's faith first came from his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice; Paul carried that heritage forward and called him “my beloved child.” Paul's verdict on him: he was “like-minded” with me, seeking not his own interests but the things of Jesus Christ, and served with me “as a child serves a father.”

No one becomes a spiritual parent automatically by being older or more experienced. It means being willing to spend time and pay a price to walk with someone as they grow. Timothy later shepherded the church in Ephesus, and Paul's life carried on through him. Here is the mindset change: a spiritual parent is not a title but a love that is willing to give itself.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The “3” of 235 is the passing on of life between spiritual parents and children. Paul and Timothy were of one mind, both focused on “the things of Jesus Christ,” not on “their own” — this is the self-emptied way of passing on life: not making disciples of ourselves but disciples of Christ, so that Jesus receives all the glory.
q: Who is God? — God shaped Timothy through three generations: Lois, Eunice and Paul. What does that show you about his patience?
Who am I? — Do you have spiritual parents in your life? And are you playing that role in someone else's life?
How shall I respond? — How will you thank a spiritual elder this week, or reach out a hand to a younger believer?
lessons.jesus: At the Last Supper Jesus called his disciples “little children” (John 13:33), giving them parting words like a father. He spent three years with them, bore with their slowness, forgave their failures, and finally entrusted his mission to them. Jesus is the source and model of all spiritual parenting.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for placing spiritual elders in my life who have walked with me in love and patience. Make me like Timothy, seeking not my own interests but the things of Jesus Christ; and one day make me like Paul, passing life on to the next generation. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write a short note of thanks to a spiritual elder
Pray for a believer younger than you, asking the Lord for an opportunity to walk with them
Read 2 Timothy 1 and circle the names Paul uses for Timothy
lessons.noon: “For they all seek their own, not the things of Jesus Christ.” — Lord, right now make me seek only your things.

lessons.title: Elijah and Elisha
lessons.theme: Those who follow to the end receive a double portion of the Spirit

v: When they had gone over, Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I shall do for you, before I am taken from you.” Elisha said, “Please let a double portion of your spirit be on me.”
He said, “You have asked a hard thing. If you see me when I am taken from you, it will be so for you; but if not, it will not be so.”
As they continued on and talked, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

lessons.still: Quietly picture Elisha hearing three times, “Please wait here,” and answering three times, “I will not leave you.” Ask yourself, “Do I long to follow like that?” Say to the Lord, “Lord, I do not want to stop halfway.”
teach: An apprentice who only looks at the finished product after his master has gone home will never learn the real craft. He has to stay at his side all day, watching how he chooses materials, how he makes the cut, how he fixes a mistake. Elisha was that kind of apprentice: from the day he left his oxen to follow Elijah, he followed him all the way to the end.

Three times Elijah told Elisha to stay behind, and three times Elisha said, “I will not leave you.” At last Elijah asked, “What shall I do for you?” Elisha asked not for wealth or position but, “Let a double portion of your spirit be on me” — he wanted a spiritual inheritance. As Elijah was taken up, he cried out, “My father, my father!” To him Elijah was not just a teacher but a father.

Spiritual inheritance takes two parties: one willing to lead, one willing to follow. Children need longing and perseverance; parents need to open up their lives for others to follow. Most important of all, what Elisha inherited was not Elijah's fame but the Spirit who moved Elijah — the heart of any spiritual inheritance is always God himself.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The Holy Spirit is my guide — what spiritual parents pass on is not their own influence but the work of the Holy Spirit. Elijah did not cling to Elisha, and Elisha did not idolise Elijah; the focus stayed on God throughout. Only this kind of inheritance lets each generation surpass the last as we build God's kingdom system.
q: Who is God? — The Spirit who moved Elijah, and moved Elisha in double measure — is he willing to move you today too?
Who am I? — Are you a spiritual child who longs to follow and keeps on to the end?
How shall I respond? — Like Elisha, what spiritual inheritance will you ask the Lord for?
lessons.jesus: As he was leaving, Jesus told his disciples, “It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I don't go away, the Counselor won't come to you.” After Elijah was taken up, Elisha received a double portion of the spirit; after Jesus ascended, the Holy Spirit was poured out on the disciples, and the gospel spread from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.
lessons.pray: Lord, I long to follow to the end like Elisha, not stopping halfway. Give me spiritual elders I can learn from, and above all, let your Spirit move me in double measure. And one day, let me pass on to the next generation, holding nothing back, all that I have received from you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down one spiritual quality you most long to inherit
Ask a spiritual elder for advice on something you are currently learning
Today, see one small thing through to the end instead of giving up halfway
lessons.noon: “Please let a double portion of your spirit be on me.” — Lord, right now fill me with your Spirit.

lessons.title: The Heart of a Spiritual Parent
lessons.theme: Caring not for applause, but only that Christ be formed in others

v: I don’t write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.
For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.
My little children, of whom I am again in travail until Christ is formed in you—

lessons.still: Place your hand over your heart and ask the Lord to put his heart into yours. Quietly think of a young believer or new Christian you care about, and say to the Lord, “Lord, give me a parent's heart for them, not just a teacher's.”
teach: A tutor cares about a student's grades and can go home when the bell rings; parents care about the child as a person, and when the child runs a fever at night they keep watch by the bed. Paul says, “Though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don't have many fathers.” The church is not short of people who can teach; it is short of people willing to be parents.

Paul uses two powerful images: “In Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News” — like a father; “I am again in travail until Christ is formed in you” — like a mother. When the Galatians went astray, Paul did not give up; he went through the pains of labour all over again. A parent's heart is persevering, costly, and aimed at the other person's growth.

The goal of spiritual parents is not for their children to become “like me” but for “Christ to be formed” in them. Here is the mindset change: I am not building my own followers; I am walking with someone as they grow into the likeness of Christ. That takes patient waiting, because growth can never be forced.
lessons.light: 321 Light: A spiritual parent's heart is a self-emptied heart — not seeking a reputation, not demanding anything back from the children, longing only for Christ to be formed in them. Letting Jesus reign means not making myself king in my children's lives; letting Jesus receive the glory means giving the Lord the credit for their growth.
q: Who is God? — With what patience has the heavenly Father waited for Christ to be formed in you?
Who am I? — Toward the younger believers around you, are you more like a “tutor” or a “parent”?
How shall I respond? — For whom are you willing to “go through labour pains,” praying and walking with them over time?
lessons.jesus: Jesus lamented over Jerusalem: “How often I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you refused!” He had a parent's heart; even when rejected, he still wept and still loved.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, put your tender heart within me. Toward the young believers around me, let me not only teach but also show a parent's love and patience. I am willing to go through labour pains for them until Christ is formed in them. Glory to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Choose one young believer and pray for them every day this week
Show interest in one thing in their everyday life, not only in their spiritual progress
Write down one quality of Christ you hope to see formed in them
lessons.noon: “Of whom I am again in travail until Christ is formed in you—” — Lord, right now give me a parent's heart.

lessons.title: Accompanying, Not Controlling
lessons.theme: Spiritual parents are examples, not lords

v: We don’t control your faith, but are fellow workers with you for your joy. For you stand firm in faith.
shepherd the flock of God which is among you, exercising the oversight, not under compulsion, but voluntarily; not for dishonest gain, but willingly;
not as lording it over those entrusted to you, but making yourselves examples to the flock.

lessons.still: Clench your fist, then let your fingers relax one by one. Think of the person you care about and say to the Lord, “Lord, they are yours, not mine. I let go, and let you be their Lord.”
teach: A father teaching his child to ride a bicycle first runs alongside holding the back of the seat; once the child is steady, he quietly lets go and watches from behind. If he never lets go, the child will never learn; if he lets go at the very start, the child will take a bad fall. The wisdom of accompanying lies in knowing when to hold on and when to let go.

Though Paul was an apostle, he said, “Not that we have lordship over your faith, but are fellow workers with you for your joy.” Peter likewise reminded the elders: “not as lording it over those entrusted to you, but making yourselves examples to the flock.” The purpose of spiritual authority is to serve, not to dominate; a spiritual parent's influence comes from example, not from commands.

Control is rooted in the self-ruled life: fear of losing influence, wanting the other person to do things my way, treating their success as my achievement. Accompanying flows from the self-emptied life: respecting the other person as God's child and helping them hear from God directly rather than depend on me. Here is the mindset change: the best spiritual parents are those whose children lean more and more on God and need them less and less.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Pride is grasping power; humility is laying down power and returning to our place. The moment spiritual parents want to be king over their children, they have left their place and taken God's. Let people be people and let God be God — let Jesus reign in my children's lives, while I simply walk alongside.
q: Who is God? — God gives people freedom and does not force them. What kind of love does that show?
Who am I? — In your relationships (children, group members, co-workers), when do you tend to slide from accompanying into controlling?
How shall I respond? — In which relationship do you need to “let go” and give the person back to the Lord?
lessons.jesus: When the rich young man went away sorrowful, Jesus did not run after him and pressure him. When many disciples turned back, Jesus asked the Twelve, “You don't also want to go away, do you?” He gave people real freedom. His authority was immense, yet he never lorded it over anyone; he drew people to follow him by love.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I sometimes want to control others and make them go my way. Forgive my self-rule, and teach me to be an example rather than a master. I place the people I care about into your hands; they are yours. May you reign in their lives. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: In one relationship today, give one less instruction and ask one more question
Speak a word of trust and affirmation to someone you often want to correct
Write down the one person you find hardest to let go of, and pray them into the Lord's hands
lessons.noon: “We don’t control your faith, but are fellow workers with you for your joy.” — Lord, right now teach me to accompany, not control.

lessons.title: Becoming a Spiritual Parent to Others
lessons.theme: Entrusting what we have received to the next generation

v: You therefore, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same things to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.
As you know, we exhorted, comforted, and implored every one of you, as a father does his own children,
to the end that you should walk worthily of God, who calls you into his own Kingdom and glory.

lessons.still: Quietly count what you have received from the Lord: salvation, his word, the faithfulness you have experienced. With each one, say, “Lord, thank you.” Finally ask, “Lord, to whom do you want me to entrust all this?”
teach: In a relay race, victory depends not only on who runs fastest but on whether the baton is passed cleanly. However fast a runner is, if he drops the baton the whole team loses. Faith is a relay too: if we do not pass on what we have received to the next runner, it stops in our hands.

2 Timothy 2:2 contains four generations: Paul (“the things … from me”), Timothy (“you have heard”), faithful people (“commit the same things”), and others (“teach others also”). Paul's vision reached beyond Timothy to his spiritual grandchildren and great-grandchildren. And the starting point of it all is verse 1: “Be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus” — passing on the faith depends on grace, not on our own strength.

You do not need to be perfect to be a spiritual parent; you only need to be one step ahead and willing to turn back and give someone a hand. Paul, like a father, “exhorted, comforted, and implored” — there was encouragement, comfort and challenge. Ask the Lord to show you one person you can walk with. Next week we learn something every spiritual parent needs: being a witness for the Lord.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The last of the eight steps of changing our mindset is Multiplication. Our one purpose — building what belongs to God — is built in exactly this way, one generation passing it on to the next. What we hand on is not ourselves but the grace we have received in Jesus; so the glory goes not to me but to Jesus.
q: Who is God? — God has entrusted the gospel to ordinary people, generation after generation. What kind of trust does that show?
Who am I? — In the relay of faith, are you the runner where the baton stops, or the one who passes it on?
How shall I respond? — Ask the Lord to show you who is the “faithful person” you can begin walking with.
lessons.jesus: Jesus spent only a little over three years on earth, focusing on walking with twelve disciples, especially Peter, James and John. He did not chase crowds; he invested his life deeply in a few. The church throughout the world today has been passed down, runner by runner, from those twelve men.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for passing the baton of the gospel into my hands through so many people. I do not want it to stop with me. Make me strong in grace, show me one faithful person, and let me exhort, comfort and urge them on as a father would. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the name of one person you could begin walking with
This week invite them for coffee or give them a call to see how they are doing
Memorise 2 Timothy 2:2 and think about who the four generations are
lessons.noon: “Commit the same things to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.” — Lord, right now show me the next runner.

mem.t: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”

lessons.title: Power When the Spirit Comes
lessons.theme: Witness depends not on eloquence but on the power of the Holy Spirit

v: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”
Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and had perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marveled. They recognized that they had been with Jesus.

lessons.still: Quietly admit, “Lord, I have no power of my own to be your witness. I am often timid, and I cannot find the words.” Then breathe in slowly, as though receiving a fresh breath: “Holy Spirit, fill me.”
teach: However beautiful a new car is, it will not move with an empty tank; fill it up, and even the most ordinary car can hit the road. Before Jesus ascended, the disciples had three years of following him and had seen the risen Lord with their own eyes — yet Jesus told them to wait first. Without the power of the Holy Spirit, witness has no fuel.

Acts 1:8 has a clear order: first “the Holy Spirit has come upon you,” then “you will receive power,” and the result is “you will be witnesses to me,” reaching from Jerusalem, Judea and Samaria to the ends of the earth — from near to far. Notice it says “you will be witnesses”: witness is first of all an identity, then an action. Acts 4:13 records that when the rulers saw the boldness of Peter and John, “they recognized that they had been with Jesus.”

Many people are afraid to bear witness because they think it takes eloquence, education or a great deal of Bible knowledge. Yet Peter and John were “unlearned and ignorant men.” The power to witness comes not from us but from the Holy Spirit; the content of our witness is not how spiritual we are but that we “have been with Jesus.” Here is the mindset change: I am not a salesperson; I am a witness — I simply tell honestly what I have seen and experienced.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The Holy Spirit is my guide — bearing witness is the Spirit's work, and we are only vessels. Live from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself; relying on the Spirit brings boldness, relying on ourselves brings pressure. The focus of witness is Jesus, not me; when people “recognise that we have been with Jesus,” Jesus receives the glory.
q: Who is God? — The Holy Spirit gave power to “unlearned and ignorant men.” How might he want to use you?
Who am I? — What is your biggest obstacle to bearing witness — fear, not knowing what to say, or feeling you are not good enough?
How shall I respond? — How will you rely on the Holy Spirit today and take a step toward your “Jerusalem”?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was baptised, the Holy Spirit came upon him; he returned from the Jordan “full of the Holy Spirit,” and went back to Galilee “in the power of the Spirit” to begin preaching (Luke 4:1, 14). Even the Son of God, in his humanity, relied on the Spirit's power to serve — and he has given us the same Spirit.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, I confess that I am often timid and want to rely on my own eloquence. Fill me; give me power and boldness, so that the people around me will recognise in me that I have been with Jesus. Beginning with my home and my workplace, make me a witness for the Lord. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Ask the Holy Spirit to give you an opportunity to share about the Lord today
Write down your “Jerusalem”: the three people you are in contact with most
Memorise Acts 1:8
lessons.noon: “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you.” — Lord, right now fill me with your Spirit.

lessons.title: The Samaritan Woman's Witness
lessons.theme: Those who meet the Lord naturally bring others to meet him

v: So the woman left her water pot, went away into the city, and said to the people,
“Come, see a man who told me everything that I have done. Can this be the Christ?”
From that city many of the Samaritans believed in him because of the word of the woman, who testified, “He told me everything that I have done.”

lessons.still: Imagine you are the one who came to draw water at noon, carrying an empty jar. Jesus sits by the well looking at you; he knows your whole past, yet he does not turn away. Quietly receive that love which sees you and still welcomes you.
teach: Someone who has just eaten at a wonderful restaurant needs no training to tell friends, “You have to go there!” They don't need to be a food critic; they only need to have tasted it themselves. Witness is like that: the most powerful testimonies often come from people who have just tasted the Lord's grace.

This woman came to draw water at noon, most likely to avoid other people. Yet Jesus broke through barriers of race, gender and morality to talk with her, told her about her past, and revealed that he was the Christ. She “left her water pot” — her original purpose was replaced by a far greater discovery. She ran back to the very people she had been avoiding and said, “Come, see!” She did not preach; she simply invited — and “many of the Samaritans believed.”

Her witness had three marks. It was honest — she told how the Lord knew her. It was humble — “Can this be the Christ?” — not forcing, only inviting. And it pointed to Jesus — in the end the people said they believed “not because of your speaking,” but because they had heard him themselves (4:42). Here is the mindset change: a witness's task is not to persuade people but to bring them to see Jesus.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The Samaritan woman did not cover up her past; she let it become a testimony to grace — this is self-emptied witness: caring not about saving face, only about glorifying the Lord. Good witness ends with people saying “not because of you”; the focus shifts from the witness to Jesus, so that Jesus receives all the glory.
q: Who is God? — What kind of Lord waits by a well for a woman everyone else avoided?
Who am I? — Do you have a “water pot” that occupies your heart more than sharing about the Lord?
How shall I respond? — To whom can you say, “Come, see,” inviting them to get to know Jesus?
lessons.jesus: Jesus “needed to pass through Samaria” (John 4:4), taking a road Jews deliberately avoided, just for one person. He did not first demand that she change; he first offered her living water. Jesus is the Father's finest witness: he carried the Father's love to those on the very margins.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for finding me at my lowest, knowing everything about me and loving me still. Help me to put down my water pot, no longer putting my image and busyness first, and to be willing to say to those around me, “Come, see!” so that they may meet you for themselves. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down your most unforgettable experience of “being seen by the Lord”
Share that experience with a friend, and finish by inviting them to get to know the Lord for themselves
Pray for someone in your circle who is often overlooked
lessons.noon: “So the woman left her water pot, went away into the city.” — Lord, right now I set aside my own concerns to be your witness.

lessons.title: Preparing My Salvation Testimony
lessons.theme: I was blind, now I see — telling my story

v: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”
But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear,

lessons.still: Quietly go back to the days before you believed, and ask the Holy Spirit to help you remember: what was the deepest emptiness or struggle in your heart then? Then recall the moment you met the Lord and the changes that followed. Do not analyse; simply remember, and give thanks.
teach: A witness in court does not need to be a lawyer or explain the whole case; they only need to say clearly, “This is what I saw with my own eyes.” Under the Pharisees' interrogation, the man born blind could not answer every theological question, but he spoke the most powerful sentence of all: “Though I was blind, now I see.”

Peter reminds us that when anyone asks the reason for the hope within us, we should “always be ready.” The foundation of that readiness is to “sanctify the Lord in your hearts,” and the attitude is “humility and fear.” A salvation testimony can be prepared in three parts: before I believed — what kind of person I was and what need was in my heart; how I came to believe — how I met Jesus and understood the gospel; after I believed — how the Lord has changed me and what hope I have now.

As you prepare your testimony, keep it brief — something you can tell in three minutes; concrete — one or two true events, without exaggeration; and centred on Jesus — not how bad or how good you are, but how good the Lord is. And state the heart of the gospel clearly: Jesus died for my sins and rose again. Here is the mindset change: my story is not for people to see me, but for them to see the Lord.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your lifestyle changes — your testimony is a true record of that road of change. A testimony is not boasting about how I have changed but counting the grace God has accomplished in Jesus; so the glory goes not to me but to Jesus.
q: Who is God? — Looking back on your salvation, how did God show his initiative and grace?
Who am I? — Can you clearly tell your own “I used to be … now I am …”?
How shall I respond? — How will you write down and prepare your three-minute testimony today?
lessons.jesus: After Jesus healed the demon-possessed man, he did not take him along but sent him home: “Tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you” (Mark 5:19). The Lord wanted not a sermon but the true story of someone who had received mercy.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for opening my eyes and bringing me out of darkness into light. Help me shape my salvation testimony — brief, true and centred on you. When someone asks me the reason for the hope within me, let me answer with humility and reverence. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write your testimony in three parts: before, how, and now
Read your testimony aloud with a timer and trim it to under three minutes
Share your salvation testimonies with each other with your spiritual companion
lessons.noon: “That though I was blind, now I see.” — Lord, right now I remember your grace.

lessons.title: Life Is the Best Witness
lessons.theme: Good deeds are light that leads people to glorify God

v: “You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden.
Neither do you light a lamp and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house.
Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
having good behavior among the nations, so in that of which they speak against you as evildoers, they may see your good works and glorify God in the day of visitation.

lessons.still: Imagine you are holding a lamp in your hands, and the Lord says, “Put it on the lampstand.” Quietly go over the places you will be today and set the lamp down in each one: the family dinner table, your seat at work, the messages on your phone.
teach: A lighthouse does not run around knocking on ships' doors saying, “Please look at me.” It simply stands there and shines, and ships lost in the storm naturally steer toward its light. The Christian life is like that: true light speaks for itself.

Jesus said, “You are the light of the world,” not “You must try hard to become light” — it is a declaration of identity. The purpose of light is not for people to look at the lamp but “that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.” Peter says that even when slandered, our good deeds will eventually lead people to “glorify God.” Life and words are the two legs of witness; we need both.

Living witness is not performing perfection; it is responding differently in ordinary situations: not retaliating when wronged, staying honest under pressure, giving thanks when others complain, admitting it when we make a mistake. Here is the mindset change: my life may be the only Bible the people around me ever read. When our words are confirmed by our lives, our witness has power.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The fivefold change — mindset, life, lifestyle, relationships, ministry — becomes visible in living witness. 920 is exactly where living witness happens: before each “2,” living out the “0” of the self-emptied life and bearing the “9,” the fruit of the Spirit. What people see is not me, but the Father in heaven.
q: Who is God? — God calls you “the light of the world.” What trust and identity does that convey?
Who am I? — When people around you look at your life, do they see light or shadow?
How shall I respond? — In what specific situation today will you let your light shine?
lessons.jesus: On the cross Jesus prayed for those who crucified him. The centurion standing opposite saw how he died and said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!” (Mark 15:39). The life Jesus lived in his most agonising moment was itself the most powerful witness.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for making me the light of the world; I do not want to hide my lamp under a basket. Help me to live, at home, at work and online, a life that matches my words, so that people may see my good works and give glory to the Father in heaven. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Today at work or at home, replace one complaint with thanksgiving
Do one act of loving service for someone you see often
Review in the evening: when was I light today, and when was I shadow?
lessons.noon: “You are the light of the world.” — Lord, right now let your light shine through me.

lessons.title: Praying for and Sharing with One Person
lessons.theme: Talk to God about them first, then talk to them about God

v: Continue steadfastly in prayer, watching in it with thanksgiving,
praying together for us also, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in bonds,
that I may reveal it as I ought to speak.
Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time.
Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one.

lessons.still: Wait quietly and ask the Holy Spirit to bring one person's name to mind — a family member, colleague or friend. Don't rush to do anything; simply bring them before the Lord and say, “Lord, you love them — more than I do.”
teach: A farmer does not sow and reap on the same day. He ploughs, sows, waters, and then waits patiently. Sharing the gospel is the same: first talk to God about the person — pray; then talk to the person about God — share; and then wait for the Holy Spirit to work.

While in chains, Paul asked the Colossians to “continue steadfastly in prayer” and to pray “that God may open to us a door for the word.” Even an apostle needed prayer to open doors! Then he taught how to relate to outsiders: “redeeming the time,” walking “in wisdom,” with speech “always with grace, seasoned with salt.” Salt gives food flavour and keeps it from spoiling; our words should make people feel warmth while also carrying weight.

This week's practice is simple: choose one person and pray three things for them every day — that God would open their heart, open a door for conversation, and open my mouth to speak fitting words. When the door opens, share naturally using the testimony you have prepared. This week we have learned to be witnesses; next week we will learn to lead people in reading God's word, helping them come to know the Lord for themselves through Scripture.
lessons.light: 321 Light: First with God, then with people — talking to God about them first, then talking to them about God; this is the spiritual order. People matter more than tasks: sharing the gospel is not completing a task but loving a person. The focus is on Jesus, not on results; the sowing is ours, but it is God who gives the growth.
q: Who is God? — God “opens a door for the word.” How might he want to open a door for the people around you?
Who am I? — Is your speech “always with grace, seasoned with salt”?
How shall I respond? — Which person will you pray for every day while waiting for an opportunity to share?
lessons.jesus: After Andrew met Jesus, he first found his own brother Simon and told him, “We have found the Messiah!” — and brought him to Jesus (John 1:41–42). One person bringing one person: and Peter, the one who was brought, later preached a single sermon at Pentecost through which three thousand turned to the Lord.
lessons.pray: Lord, I bring the friend on my heart before you; you love them more deeply than I do. Open their heart, open a door for conversation, and give me words full of grace and seasoned with salt. Let me talk to you about them first, then talk to them about you, and leave the outcome in your hands. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down one name as your gospel prayer focus for this season
Pray three things for them every day: open heart, open door, open mouth
Look for a chance this week to show you care, and share your three-minute testimony
lessons.noon: “Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt.” — Lord, right now let my words carry your grace.

mem.t: Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness, that each person who belongs to God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.

lessons.title: Philip and the Eunuch
lessons.theme: Leading someone in Bible reading means helping them find Jesus in the Scriptures

v: Philip ran to him, and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said, “Do you understand what you are reading?”
He said, “How can I, unless someone explains it to me?” He begged Philip to come up and sit with him.
Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, preached to him about Jesus.

lessons.still: Imagine you are the eunuch sitting in the chariot reading Scripture you cannot understand, longing for someone to come and read it with you. Then think of someone around you who also cannot understand it. Say to the Lord, “Lord, send me like Philip to climb into their chariot.”
teach: Some people have a beautiful Bible at home; they open it, read a few pages, and put it down. It is not that they don't want to read it — they don't understand it, and no one is reading with them. It is like being handed a map in a foreign language with no one to explain the legend. What many people need is not more Bibles but someone to read with them.

Philip was led to the desert, “ran” to the chariot, and began with a good question: “Do you understand what you are reading?” The eunuch answered honestly: “How can I, unless someone explains it to me?” and invited Philip to “come up and sit with him.” Philip, “beginning from this Scripture” — starting from the very passage the man was reading — “preached to him about Jesus.” The focus of reading Scripture with someone is not knowledge but Jesus.

From Philip we learn four steps for leading someone in Bible reading: follow the Holy Spirit's leading, take the initiative to come close, begin with a question, and point from the text to Jesus. Here is the mindset change: leading Bible reading is not running a class; it is “climbing into the chariot and sitting alongside” — sitting next to someone, starting from where they are, and finding Jesus in the Scriptures together.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The three foundations come together in Philip — the Holy Spirit led him there (the Holy Spirit is my guide), he began from the Scripture (Scripture is my standard), and he preached Jesus (Jesus is my example). The purpose of reading Scripture with others is not for them to admire how much I know, but for them to meet Jesus.
q: Who is God? — What kind of God sends Philip into the desert for the sake of one person?
Who am I? — Do you have passages you “don't understand but are afraid to say so,” or have you been helped by someone reading with you?
How shall I respond? — Whom could you invite to “sit alongside” you and read a passage of Scripture?
lessons.jesus: On the road to Emmaus the risen Jesus, “beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself” (Luke 24:27). The whole Bible points to Jesus; leading Bible reading means following the Lord and bringing people before the One the Scriptures point to.
lessons.pray: Lord, make me like Philip — sensitive to the Holy Spirit's leading, willing to run over, sit down, and read your word with someone. Not to show what I know, but so that people may see you in the Scriptures. Bring someone who is hungry for you across my path. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Ask a friend, “Is there anything in your Bible reading lately that you haven't understood?”
Invite someone to read a passage from the Gospels with you this week
Read Acts 8:26–40 and mark each of Philip's actions
lessons.noon: “Do you understand what you are reading?” — Lord, right now send me to help someone understand your word.

lessons.title: Ezra Teaches the Law
lessons.theme: Study first, then obey, then teach

v: For Ezra had set his heart to seek the LORD’s law, and to do it, and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel.
They read in the book, in the law of God, distinctly; and they gave the sense, so that they understood the reading.

lessons.still: Lay your Bible on your lap and rest your hands gently on it. Say to the Lord, “Lord, I want to let your word teach me first, before I teach others.” Be still for a moment and ask the Lord to place one verse in your heart.
teach: If a chef never tastes his own cooking and only teaches from the recipe, his students will soon notice that he cannot describe the layers of flavour. Teaching God's word is the same: those who have not first been fed by the word will find it hard to pass on its taste to others.

Ezra 7:10 gives the teacher's three steps: “seek” — study carefully; “do it” — live it out first; “teach” — then instruct others. The order cannot be reversed. In Nehemiah 8, Ezra and the Levites read before the people “distinctly,” “gave the sense,” “so that they understood” — reading, explaining, understanding, so that God's word entered people's hearts. The people first wept, then rejoiced greatly, because they had understood God's word.

Those who lead Bible reading need not be theologians, but they must be “those who read first.” Here is the mindset change: I teach what I have lived, not only what I know. When preparing to lead others, first ask yourself: what is this passage saying to me? Have I obeyed it? Only then ask: how can I help others understand and obey it?
lessons.light: 321 Light: The eight steps of changing our mindset — Information, Revelation, Conviction, Practice, Review, Correction, Repetition, Multiplication. Ezra walked through the first seven steps before moving into Multiplication by teaching others. Scripture is my standard: it is not I who teach people, but God's word speaking for itself, helping people understand and obey.
q: Who is God? — God wants people to “understand” his word, not just hear it. What does that show you about his heart?
Who am I? — Is your Bible reading more like careful “seeking” or quick skimming? How much of it have you obeyed?
How shall I respond? — Which passage will you “seek and do” this week, in preparation for teaching in the future?
lessons.jesus: The crowds were astonished at Jesus' teaching, for he taught with authority and not like the scribes (Mark 1:22). What he taught was what he lived: he taught people to pray, and he himself prayed often; he taught people to love their enemies, and he himself interceded for those who crucified him. His words and life were perfectly one, and so they carried authority.
lessons.pray: Lord, make me like Ezra, setting my heart to study, obey and teach your word. Forgive me for so often wanting to teach others without first letting your word change me. Open my heart; let me first be fed by your word, and then pass its taste on to others. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Choose a passage, read it three times today, and write down what it says to you
Identify one concrete way you can obey this passage today
“Give the sense” to a companion by explaining the passage in your own words
lessons.noon: “For Ezra had set his heart to seek the LORD’s law, and to do it” — Lord, right now help me obey your word first.

lessons.title: How to Lead a Bible Study
lessons.theme: Observe, interpret, apply — and let people discover for themselves

v: Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,
that each person who belongs to God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.
Now these were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, examining the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.

lessons.still: Open your Bible, choose a familiar verse, and read it slowly three times, each time slower than the last. The first time, notice the words; the second time, their meaning; the third time, yourself. Wait quietly for the Lord to shine his light on one word.
teach: Give a man a fish and he eats for a day; teach him to fish and he eats for a lifetime. The goal of leading Bible reading is not to feed others your own insights but to help them learn to be fed from Scripture themselves. A good Bible study leader is like a fishing coach who lets people reel in their first fish with their own hands.

Paul says that every Scripture is “God-breathed” and profitable for teaching, reproof, correction and instruction in righteousness, so that the one who belongs to God “may be complete.” The Bereans “received the word with all readiness of the mind, examining the Scriptures daily” — readiness is the attitude, daily is the habit, examining is the method. Bible study is examining together: what exactly has God said?

A simple method has three steps. Observe: what does the passage say? Who, what, when, where. Interpret: what does it mean? Look at the context and what it meant to its first readers. Apply: how does God want me to respond? Turn it into one concrete action. In a small-group study, the leader should talk less and ask more, letting everyone discover the truth in the text for themselves.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Scripture is my standard — Bible study is not swapping personal opinions but returning together to God's word.
