Information becomes practice only through the Holy Spirit's revelation and the heart's conviction; so the destination of Bible study is always application, letting God's word change our mindset, our life and our lifestyle.
q: Who is God? — God gave his inspired word so that we may “be complete.” What does that show about his heart?
Who am I? — When you read the Bible, do you usually stop at observation and interpretation, or go on to application?
How shall I respond? — Which passage will you study using the three steps of observe, interpret and apply?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was tempted in the wilderness, he answered three times, “It is written.” In debates he often brought people back to the text itself. He held God's word as the highest standard and taught his disciples to return to the Scriptures. Jesus is the best Bible reader of all; he brings people face to face with God's word.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for the God-breathed Scriptures that make me complete. Give me the Bereans' ready heart and their habit of examining the Scriptures daily. And teach me, when I lead others, to speak less and ask more, so that everyone may be fed from your word for themselves. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Study Acts 17:11 using the three steps of observe, interpret and apply
Write down one concrete application you will obey today
Invite a friend to read a passage together using these three steps next time you meet
lessons.noon: “Every Scripture is God-breathed.” — Lord, right now let your word be my standard.

lessons.title: Asking Good Questions
lessons.theme: A good question opens a door to discovery

v: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?”
Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”

lessons.still: Quietly hear Jesus ask you, “Who do you say that I am?” Don't rush to recite the standard answer; answer honestly in your heart: today, who is he to me? Let the question rest in your heart for a minute.
teach: A good doctor does not prescribe medicine the moment you walk in; first they ask: where does it hurt? When did it start? Good questions uncover the real cause. Leading Bible reading is the same: giving answers only passes on information, but asking questions lets people discover the truth for themselves — and truth we discover ourselves is the hardest to forget.

Jesus was a master of questions. First he asked, “Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?” Then, “But who do you say that I am?” — moving from other people's opinions to a personal response. When an expert in the law tested him, he asked in return, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?” — bringing the man back to the text itself, and to his own understanding of it.

Good questions have several marks. They are open — they cannot be answered with just yes or no. They are anchored in the text — the clues to the answer are in the passage. They touch life — “What does this mean for you?” For example: “What does this passage show you about what God is like?” “Which sentence touches you most, and why?” Here is the mindset change: a leader is not an answer machine but a curious companion.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Asking questions is humble leadership — not monopolising the pulpit, but letting people be people and letting God be God. A self-emptied leader can wait patiently and respect each person's discovery; the focus is not on showing what I know but on letting the Holy Spirit use the questions to shine light into hearts, turning people from “the things of men” to “the things of God.”
q: Who is God? — Jesus asks, “Who do you say that I am?” What kind of relationship does that show he longs to have with you?
Who am I? — In your small group or at home, do you more often give answers or ask questions?
How shall I respond? — What good question will you use today to help someone reflect more deeply on God's word?
lessons.jesus: At twelve years old, Jesus was found in the temple “sitting in the middle of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions” (Luke 2:46). After his resurrection he asked Mary Magdalene, “Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?” His questions always gently drew out what was deep in people's hearts, and then they met him.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for gently knocking on the door of my heart with your questions. When I lead others, help me lecture less and listen more, and ask good questions that open hearts. May the Holy Spirit use these questions so that people come to know for themselves that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Prepare three open-ended questions for your next small group or family Bible reading
In one conversation today, ask one more question and give one less piece of advice
Honestly write down your answer to “Who do you say that I am?”
lessons.noon: “But who do you say that I am?” — Lord, right now I say: you are the Christ, my Lord.

lessons.title: Let the Holy Spirit Be the Teacher
lessons.theme: The One who truly opens hearts is the Spirit of truth

v: But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you.

However, when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears, he will speak. He will declare to you things that are coming.

lessons.still: Before reading Scripture, pause and lay your open hands on your Bible. Say, “Holy Spirit, you are my teacher; open my mind.” Don't rush to read; let your heart grow quiet first, like a student waiting for the teacher to speak.
teach: Even the best tutor cannot understand for the student. He can explain, give examples and set exercises, but the moment of “I get it” happens inside the student. Spiritual understanding is even more so: we can explain a passage, but only the Holy Spirit can turn on the light in someone's heart.

Jesus promised that the Counsellor, the Holy Spirit, “will teach you all things” and “will remind you of all that I said to you”; he is “the Spirit of truth,” who “will guide you into all truth.” Notice that the Spirit “will not speak from himself” — he always glorifies Christ and brings people back to the words of Jesus. So the Spirit's guidance will never contradict Scripture.

This week we learned to draw near from Philip and to obey first from Ezra; we learned to observe, interpret and apply, and to ask good questions. Today's summary is this: methods are vessels; the Holy Spirit is the Teacher. Pray before you lead, wait on him while you lead, and trust him when you are done. Next week we will learn to pray together in one accord, experiencing this same Spirit together in prayer.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Live from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself; the heart brings gladness, the head brings worry. Those who lead Bible reading and try to make people understand by their own effort will grow anxious; those who let the Holy Spirit be the teacher can rest. Scripture is the standard, the Holy Spirit is the guide, Jesus is the focus — the three foundations become one as we read the Bible.
q: Who is God? — The Holy Spirit “will guide you into all truth.” How is he with you right now?
Who am I? — When you share God's word, do you rely on the Holy Spirit, or on your own preparation and eloquence?
How shall I respond? — How will you invite the Holy Spirit to be your teacher each time you read Scripture this week?
lessons.jesus: The risen Jesus “opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures” (Luke 24:45). After three years of following the Lord the disciples still did not understand, until the risen Lord opened their minds and the Holy Spirit came at Pentecost; then they spoke boldly of Christ from the Scriptures. Today this same Spirit opens our minds too.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, you are the Spirit of truth and my teacher. Forgive me for so often trying to understand by myself and teach others by myself. Open my mind, and the minds of those I lead, so that we may understand the truth and love Jesus more. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Each time before reading Scripture, invite the Holy Spirit to be your teacher in one sentence
While reading, note one of the Lord's words that the Holy Spirit “reminds” you of
Pray for the companion or small group you will pray with next week
lessons.noon: “He will guide you into all truth” — Lord, right now let your Spirit be my teacher.

mem.t: Again, assuredly I tell you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven. For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”

lessons.title: Continuing Steadfastly in Prayer with One Accord
lessons.theme: The church was born out of a prayer meeting

v: All these with one accord continued steadfastly in prayer and supplication, along with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brothers.
They continued steadfastly in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer.

lessons.still: Imagine yourself in that upper room in Jerusalem, waiting with the hundred and twenty. No one is rushing to get things done; everyone is simply praying together. Quietly join them and say to the Lord, “Lord, I am willing to wait for you together with my brothers and sisters.”
teach: Before an orchestra begins, all the musicians tune together; if they are out of tune, no amount of skill produces anything but noise. Before Pentecost the early church “tuned up” in prayer — they “with one accord continued steadfastly in prayer,” waiting for the Holy Spirit the Father had promised.

The group in Acts 1:14 was diverse: the apostles, several women, Jesus' mother, and his brothers who had once not believed in him. What they shared was being “of one accord” and “steadfast.” After Pentecost the newborn church still “continued steadfastly in the apostles' teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer” — prayer was not an occasional activity but the rhythm of the church's life.

We often think of prayer as a private matter, but in Scripture prayer is also the breathing of the community. Here is the mindset change: praying in one accord is not adding up individual prayers; it is a group of people tuning together to the heart of God. Private prayer builds intimacy with God; united prayer builds a community that belongs to God.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Our one purpose — building God's kingdom system — was born in prayer. Being of one accord requires each person to live the self-emptied life: laying down our own agendas and tuning together to God's will. Pride makes everyone talk past each other; humility brings people into one accord, and the Holy Spirit works among them.
q: Who is God? — Why did God choose to pour out his Spirit on a group of people praying with one accord?
Who am I? — Is your prayer life more like a solo or an ensemble?
How shall I respond? — Which time of united prayer can you join or start this week?
lessons.jesus: Before his ascension Jesus told his disciples not to leave Jerusalem but to wait for what the Father had promised (Acts 1:4). He did not tell them each to go home and wait, but to wait together. The prayer the Lord taught also begins with “our”: “Our Father in heaven” — from the very start, prayer is a family matter.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often pray only for myself and seldom pray in one accord with my brothers and sisters. Make me willing to lay down my own agenda and pray steadfastly with your people, of one heart and mind. May your church be filled with you as we pray. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Check this week's prayer meetings at your church or small group and plan to attend
Send a message to a brother or sister: “Shall we pray together for five minutes?”
When you pray today, change “I” to “we”
lessons.noon: “They continued steadfastly in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer.” — Lord, right now make prayer the rhythm of my life.

lessons.title: Two or Three in Agreement
lessons.theme: The Lord promises to be among two or three gathered in his name

v: Again, assuredly I tell you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.
For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”

lessons.still: Think of one or two people you could pray with, and in your heart bring them to your side. Quietly receive the Lord's promise: “There I am in the middle of them.” The Lord is standing among you — not far away in heaven.
teach: The light of one match is faint, but put two or three together and the flame grows strong enough to light a pile of wood. The Lord did not say we must wait for hundreds of people before we pray; he said “two,” “two or three” — the smallest unit of united prayer, so small that everyone can take part.

“Agreeing” is like several instruments sounding the same chord: not just agreeing on the same thing, but hearts tuned together toward God. “In my name” means gathering according to the Lord's heart and under his authority. These words come in the context of dealing with a brother who sins, which shows that united prayer is also closely tied to restoring relationships and keeping order in the community.

This promise is not a wishing well, as if God must comply once two people have agreed. The key is “in my name” — when two or three agree under the Lord's name, what they ask becomes more and more like the Lord's heart, and the Lord himself is among them. Here is the mindset change: the greatest reward of united prayer is not just answered prayer but the Lord's presence.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The best way for “2” spiritual companions in 235 to spend time together is to pray in agreement. If one of the two is self-ruled and insists on his own way, they cannot agree; if both are self-emptied and let Jesus reign, they can be of one heart and mind. Answered prayer is for Jesus to receive the glory, not for us to feel pleased with ourselves.
q: Who is God? — The Lord promises to be among two or three. How near is this Lord to you?
Who am I? — Have you and your spiritual companion ever prayed together?
How shall I respond? — With whom will you arrange a “two or three” time of united prayer this week?
lessons.jesus: Jesus took Peter, James and John up the mountain to pray (Luke 9:28), and “as he was praying,” the appearance of his face changed. He often prayed together with a few disciples, letting them see with their own eyes the glory of his fellowship with the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for promising to be among two or three. Give me companions to pray with in agreement, and help us lay down our own ideas and be of one accord in your name. What we long for most is not only answered prayer but your presence. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Arrange with your spiritual companion to pray together for fifteen minutes this week
Each share one prayer request, and pray for one another
Memorise Matthew 18:19–20
lessons.noon: “For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.” — Lord, right now you are here among us.

lessons.title: The Power of the Prayer Meeting
lessons.theme: When the church prays earnestly, prison doors open and believers are filled with the Spirit

v: Peter therefore was kept in the prison, but constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him.
When they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were gathered together. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness.

lessons.still: Think of people around you who are “locked in prison” — trapped by illness, hardship or bondage. Quietly bring their names before the Lord. Then ask the Lord to help you see that the praying community you belong to is a channel through which God works.
teach: When a dam is full and the sluice gates open, the water drives the turbines and lights up a whole city. The prayer meeting is often seen as the least popular gathering: few people, long hours, not much buzz. In fact it is the church's “power station” — God's power is displayed through united prayer.

In Acts 12 James had been killed and Peter imprisoned; the situation was hopeless. “But constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him” — that one word “but” turned everything around. The angel of the Lord led Peter out of prison, while the people praying were gathered in Mary's house. In Acts 4, after the disciples were threatened, they prayed together, “the place was shaken,” and they were filled with the Holy Spirit and “spoke the word of God with boldness.” They did not ask for the danger to disappear; they asked for boldness.

Interestingly, when Peter knocked at the door, those praying at first did not believe it was him (12:15)! God's answer was bigger than their faith. Here is the mindset change: the power of prayer does not lie in how perfect our faith is, but in the God who hears prayer. What God values is a group of people willing to gather and come before him earnestly together.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The prayer meeting is a community act of “letting Jesus reign” — admitting we are powerless and handing the situation over to God. The focus is not how frightening the circumstances are but that Jesus is in control. In a crisis, the church does not first rely on its own solutions but prays first; this is living from the heart by the Spirit.
q: Who is God? — In the darkness of James's death and Peter's imprisonment, how did God answer the church's prayer?
Who am I? — Do you see the prayer meeting as optional, or as the church's power station?
How shall I respond? — For which person “in prison” could you invite others to pray together this week?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus cleansed the temple he quoted Scripture: “My house shall be called a house of prayer” (Matthew 21:13). In his heart, God's house is first and foremost a place of prayer. He also promised that whatever his disciples ask in his name he will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son (John 14:13).
lessons.pray: Lord, revive our prayer meetings, and forgive us for so often treating prayer as optional. We pray earnestly for brothers and sisters caught in hardship; please act on their behalf. And fill us with the Holy Spirit, so that we speak your word with boldness. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Attend this week's prayer meeting at your church or small group
For a brother or sister in difficulty, invite two or three others to pray together
Write down one prayer request, then wait for and record God's answer
lessons.noon: “But constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him.” — Lord, right now I cry out to you for those caught in hardship.

lessons.title: Praying for the Kingdom
lessons.theme: The scope of prayer widens from my needs to God's kingdom

v: Pray like this: “‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
I exhort therefore, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made for all men,
for kings and all who are in high places, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and reverence.

lessons.still: Slowly pray the first three lines of the Lord's Prayer, pausing after each line to take a deep breath. When you reach “Let your Kingdom come,” quietly imagine God's kingdom coming to your home, your city, your nation.
teach: Many people's prayers are like a shopping list: health, a job, the children… All of these are fine to ask for, but if that is all our prayer contains, it is like a window that only looks out on our own backyard. The Lord's Prayer opens a large window for us, so that we can see God's kingdom.

The Lord's Prayer puts God first and people second: first “may your name be kept holy,” then “let your Kingdom come” and “let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven,” and only then our daily bread. Paul likewise urged Timothy that “first of all, petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made for all men,” including “kings and all who are in high places.” Praying for the kingdom means asking that God's will be done in the church, in our cities and among the nations.

Praying for the kingdom can have specific scopes: for the church's pastors and workers, for the leaders and society of our city, for our nation's government, for unreached peoples, for the persecuted church. Here is the mindset change: prayer is not only God meeting my needs; it is me taking part in God's work. When we pray for the kingdom, our own needs actually find their proper place.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Building God's kingdom system means fulfilling the Lord's Prayer — hallowing his name, his kingdom coming, his will done on earth as in heaven; the kingdom, the power and the glory all belong to God. A change of perspective: from the earthly to the heavenly, from the temporary to the eternal. Praying for the kingdom is letting Jesus reign over all things.
q: Who is God? — God “desires all people to be saved.” How wide is the heart of his kingdom?
Who am I? — How much of your prayer list is for God's kingdom?
How shall I respond? — Which area of the kingdom (church, city, nation, the nations) will you pray for regularly this week?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus saw the crowds harassed and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd, he said to his disciples, “Pray therefore that the Lord of the harvest will send out laborers into his harvest” (Matthew 9:38). He did not only do the work himself; he taught his disciples to pray for the needs of God's kingdom.
lessons.pray: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy; may your kingdom come; may your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Widen the scope of my prayers, so that I intercede for the church, my city, my nation and all peoples. Yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Make a kingdom prayer list covering the church, your city, your nation and the nations
Pray today for one of your nation's leaders
Pray for an unreached people group or a persecuted church
lessons.noon: “Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.” — Lord, right now reign in me.

lessons.title: Building Prayer Partnerships
lessons.theme: Holding up each other's hands, we overcome together

v: When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed. When he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

But Moses’ hands were heavy; so they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His hands were steady until sunset.

lessons.still: Lift up both hands for a moment and feel your arms gradually grow heavy. As you lower them, ask the Lord to remind you of brothers and sisters whose “hands may be growing heavy,” and admit honestly, “Lord, I too need someone to hold up my hands.”
teach: Down in the valley Joshua was fighting; up on the hill Moses was lifting his hands. The outcome of the battle depended not on swords but on a pair of raised hands. But Moses was human, and his hands grew heavy. So Aaron and Hur brought a stone for him to sit on and held up his hands, one on each side — “His hands were steady until sunset.”

This is a picture of prayer partners: in spiritual warfare no one can keep their hands raised alone to the end. Aaron and Hur were not the main characters, yet they were key to the victory; they did not replace Moses, they held him up. Prayer partners are like that: when the other is weary, we hold them up in prayer until the victory is won.

This week we have walked through the early church's united prayer, the promise to two or three, the power of the prayer meeting, and praying for the kingdom. Today let us put it into practice by forming regular prayer partnerships — setting a time, sharing needs, praying for one another, and recording answers. Next week we will learn about the gifts of the Holy Spirit — how, like Aaron and Hur, each of us plays our part in the body of Christ and works together with others.
lessons.light: 321 Light: From the “2” spiritual companions to the “5” fellow soldiers of 235, everyone needs the support of prayer. Do not hurt people for the sake of tasks; hold people up for the sake of people. The humble admit they need support; the self-emptied are willing to be the unseen ones holding up the hands — the glory goes to God, not to ourselves.
q: Who is God? — God tied victory to a pair of hands held up by others. What does that show you about how he designed community?
Who am I? — Are you more like Moses, with heavy hands needing support, or like Aaron and Hur, able to hold others up?
How shall I respond? — With whom will you form a regular prayer partnership, supporting one another?
lessons.jesus: In the Garden of Gethsemane Jesus said to his disciples, “Stay here, and watch with me.” He longed for someone to pray with him, but the disciples fell asleep. Now “he always lives to make intercession for them” (Hebrews 7:25); he is the High Priest who forever holds up our hands.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you that you always live to intercede for me. I confess that I often try to hold on alone, and my hands have grown heavy. Give me prayer partners, and make me willing to be an Aaron or a Hur for others, holding up their hands in prayer until the victory is won. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Invite a companion to become your regular prayer partner
Agree on a weekly time to share prayer requests with each other
Start a prayer journal to record each other's needs and God's answers
lessons.noon: “Aaron and Hur held up his hands.” — Lord, right now I lift my hands in prayer for my companion.

mem.t: As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.

lessons.title: Gifts Are for Building Up the Body
lessons.theme: Gifts are not medals awarded to individuals but presents given to the body

v: Now there are various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.
There are various kinds of service, and the same Lord.
There are various kinds of workings, but the same God who works all things in all.
But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.

lessons.still: Rest your open hands on your knees and breathe quietly. Say to the Lord, “Lord, everything in my hands is something you have given.” Think back over what you have received from the Lord this year; don't rush to use any of it — first, simply give thanks.
teach: When a big family gathers for a holiday, someone cooks, someone washes up, someone chats with the grandparents, someone makes the children laugh. If everyone fought to do the cooking, the kitchen would be packed while no one was at the table looking after the guests. Gifts are like the division of tasks in a household: not for comparing who matters most, but for bringing the whole family to life.

Three times in a row Paul says “various kinds” — gifts, service and workings all differ; and three times he says “the same” — the same Spirit, the same Lord, the same God. The source of all this variety is the one triune God. Verse 7 is the key: “to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.” Gifts are not aimed inward to fulfil ourselves but outward to benefit others.

So gifts are not badges of spiritual status, nor capital for building a personal brand. Before asking, “What gifts do I have?” first ask, “For whom were they given?” Once our mindset turns — from “mine” to “the Lord's,” from “for myself” to “for the body” — gifts stop being a source of pride and become channels of service.
lessons.light: 321 Light: When gifts are seized by the self-ruled life, they become power to exalt ourselves; only when handed back to the Lord do they become building materials for God's kingdom system. When Jesus reigns, our gifts have their rightful owner; when Jesus receives the glory, our gifts have their rightful direction.
q: Who is God? — The triune God is one, yet works in such varied ways. What does that teach you about him?
Who am I? — Have you ever treated a gift as your own achievement or as a label of identity?
How shall I respond? — What has the Lord given you that you can use today for someone else's benefit?
lessons.jesus: Jesus was full of the Holy Spirit and had great power to heal, cast out demons and teach, yet he never used it to turn stones into bread for himself or to win applause. Every display of his power was for the good of others and the glory of the Father.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, thank you for giving gifts to me — not because I deserve them, but because you love your church. Remove from me any desire to use my gifts to exalt myself, and let everything in my hands become a blessing to others. May all glory be to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: List three things others have told you were “really helpful”
Write a note of thanks to someone in your church who serves quietly
Today, use something you are good at to help someone, without being asked
lessons.noon: “But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.” — Lord, right now make me a blessing to others.

lessons.title: The Picture of the Body
lessons.theme: In the body of Christ, no one is unnecessary

v: The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”
No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.
When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. When one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.

lessons.still: Slowly become aware of your body from head to toe: your eyes, your hands, your feet, and your heart, unseen yet beating all the time. Say to the Lord, “Thank you for making me, and for placing me in your body.”
teach: Your little finger seems insignificant, but catch it in a door and your whole body stops — even your voice changes. A body is never a set of independent parts; it is one life in which every part feels the others: when one place hurts, the whole body knows.

Paul is dealing with two errors here. One is “the eye can't tell the hand, ‘I have no need for you’” — thinking ourselves strong and looking down on others. The other, a little earlier, is the foot saying, “Because I'm not the hand, I'm not part of the body” — thinking ourselves weak and giving up on ourselves. The first is pride, the second self-pity, but both are focused on self. Verses 26–27 give the answer: we suffer together and rejoice together, because “you are the body of Christ.”

The church is not a collection of individual believers but a living organism. When I learn to rejoice in others' success and weep over others' pain, I am no longer a spectator sitting in a meeting but a member living in the body. This is also the soil for 235 relationships: without an awareness of the body, there can be no real companions or teams.
lessons.light: 321 Light: People matter more than tasks; relationships matter more than things. In the body, the focus is not on who is more visible but on Christ the Head. Humility lets me admit, “I need you”; the self-emptied life makes me willing to say, “Your joy is my joy” — this is a body united.
q: Who is God? — God deliberately regards the “weaker” members as indispensable. What does that show you about him?
Who am I? — Are you more likely to say “I have no need for you” or “I am not part of the body”?
How shall I respond? — Who in your church is suffering or being honoured right now, and needs you to share in it?
lessons.jesus: The risen Jesus appeared to Saul, who was persecuting the church, and said, “Why are you persecuting me?” To persecute the members is to persecute the Head. He is the Head; he feels the pain in every part of the body and intercedes before the Father for every member.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you that you are the Head and I am a member of your body. Forgive me for looking down on others, and forgive me for looking down on myself. Teach me to weep with those who weep and rejoice with those who rejoice; let me live within your body and no longer fight alone. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Say to a brother or sister you have looked down on, “I need you”
Pray specifically for a member of your church who is suffering
Sincerely congratulate a co-worker on something they have achieved
lessons.noon: “Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.” — Lord, right now let my heart beat together with your body.

lessons.title: Discovering My Gifts
lessons.theme: Thinking of ourselves soberly, and recognising our gifts as we serve

v: For I say through the grace that was given me, to everyone who is among you, not to think of yourself more highly than you ought to think; but to think reasonably, as God has apportioned to each person a measure of faith.
having gifts differing according to the grace that was given to us: if prophecy, let’s prophesy according to the proportion of our faith;
or service, let’s give ourselves to service; or he who teaches, to his teaching;
or he who exhorts, to his exhorting; he who gives, let him do it with generosity; he who rules, with diligence; he who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.

lessons.still: Become still and ask the Holy Spirit to help you remember: when have you served others and felt especially joyful inside, while they were especially helped? Don't evaluate; just let the scenes come to mind one by one, and write them down.
teach: You don't know how deep a well is just by digging it; you find out by lowering the bucket and drawing water. Many people want to “measure” their gifts first before they start serving, but gifts are often discovered in the course of serving. It is like learning to swim: however many manuals you read on the shore, you only find out whether you can float once you get in the water.

Paul first says, “not to think of yourself more highly than you ought to think; but to think reasonably,” and only then talks about gifts. Overestimating ourselves is pride; underestimating ourselves is another form of self-centredness. The gifts he lists are very down-to-earth: prophecy, service, teaching, exhorting, giving, leading, showing mercy — and each comes with an attitude: wholehearted, generous, diligent, cheerful. Gifts joined to character are what become a blessing.

There are three clues to discovering your gifts: the burden in your heart (what do I often care deeply about?), confirmation from others (how do people find me helpful?), and the fruit of the Spirit (does life flow out when I do it?). The best way is to try serving within your “2” and “3” relationships, letting your spiritual companions and spiritual parents help you see what you cannot see in yourself.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Thinking reasonably about ourselves means returning to our place — letting people be people and letting God be God. The Holy Spirit is my guide; he distributes gifts to each one. Jesus is my example; he displayed his gifts in serving. A change of mindset: no longer knowing myself through comparison, but through what God has apportioned.
q: Who is God? — God apportions “to each person a measure of faith.” What does that show you about his wisdom?
Who am I? — Are you more prone to overestimate yourself or to underestimate yourself?
How shall I respond? — Which spiritual companion or spiritual parent will you ask to tell you what gifts they see in you?
lessons.jesus: At twelve Jesus was listening, asking and answering in the temple, yet he began his public ministry only after his baptism at thirty. He knew clearly what the Father had sent him to do, so he was not driven by the crowd's expectations. The root of knowing our gifts is knowing our relationship with the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord, help me think of myself with sober judgement — neither proud nor self-deprecating. Holy Spirit, open my eyes to recognise the gifts you have placed in me, and give me a heart that is wholehearted, generous, diligent and cheerful in using them. May I be used by you, not bound by comparison. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three experiences of serving in which you felt joy and others were helped
Ask a spiritual companion to tell you what gifts they see in you
Try a small form of service this week that you have never done before
lessons.noon: “But to think reasonably” — Lord, right now let me see myself through your eyes.

lessons.title: Love Is the Most Excellent Way
lessons.theme: Without love, even the greatest gift counts for nothing

v: But earnestly desire the best gifts. Moreover, I show a most excellent way to you.
If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don’t have love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.
If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but don’t have love, I am nothing.
If I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but don’t have love, it profits me nothing.

lessons.still: Call to mind, one by one, the acts of service you will do today, and quietly place one word in front of each: “love.” Gently ask the Lord, “Am I doing this out of love, or for myself?” Then listen.
teach: Even the finest sound system, unplugged, is just a silent box; and if the current is faulty, it produces only harsh noise. Gifts are like the sound system, and love is like the current. Gifts without love are not merely useless — they can even hurt people.

The Corinthian church had many gifts yet was full of quarrels. Between chapters 12 and 14, where he discusses gifts, Paul deliberately placed a chapter on love. In one breath he lists the most admired gifts — tongues, prophecy, knowledge, mountain-moving faith, even self-sacrifice — and concludes: without love, I am a clanging cymbal, I am nothing, it profits me nothing. The most excellent way is not one more gift; it is the road every gift must travel.

Here we need a change of perspective: from “What can I do?” to “How do I love people?” The test of service is not how big the event is or how much applause there is, but whether the person being served has felt God's love. People matter more than tasks; if we hurt people for the sake of getting things done well, we have already strayed from the most excellent way.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Love is the self-emptied life — living for Jesus and for others, not for ourselves. Gifts belong to “ministry”; love belongs to “life”: life first, then relationships, then ministry. In 920, love heads the ninefold fruit of the Spirit, precisely so that our gifts operate in the soil of that fruit.
q: Who is God? — Why does God regard love as greater than every gift?
Who am I? — Have there been times in your service when you became “sounding brass or a clanging cymbal”?
How shall I respond? — In which act of service today will you choose first to love the person?
lessons.jesus: The Gospels often record that before a miracle Jesus was “moved with compassion.” When he healed a man with leprosy, he first reached out and touched him — his power healed the body, and his touch healed a heart long cut off from others. Everything he did flowed out of love.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, I confess that in my service I have sometimes cared more about results than about people. Fill me with your love, so that what I do is no longer sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. Let me love people first and then serve them; let what people sense in me be you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before an act of service begins, spend one minute praying for the person you will serve
Apologise to someone you have treated impatiently while serving
Today, offer a warm look or greeting in place of a correction
lessons.noon: “I show a most excellent way to you.” — Lord, right now let me walk in the way of love.

lessons.title: Serving One Another with Our Gifts
lessons.theme: Being good stewards of God's varied grace, so that God is glorified in all things

v: As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.

If anyone speaks, let it be as it were the very words of God. If anyone serves, let it be as of the strength which God supplies, that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.

lessons.still: Take a deep breath and imagine the Lord placing a bunch of keys in your hand, each one a gift. They are not given for you to collect, but for you to open other people's doors. Say to the Lord, “Lord, I am your steward.”
teach: A steward lives in his master's great house and holds all the keys; he can deploy every resource, yet he knows full well that none of it is his. A good steward's joy lies not in owning but in seeing the master's household run well and the master pleased.

Peter says “each” — there is no believer without a gift; “serving one another” — gifts flow within relationships; “in its various forms” — God's grace comes in a thousand shapes. Verse 11 divides gifts into two broad kinds, speaking and serving, and the principle is the same for both: speak as the very words of God, serve by the strength God supplies. And the purpose is one: “that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ.”

This week we have seen that gifts are for building up the body (Day 1), that I belong within the body (Day 2), how to recognise our gifts (Day 3), and that love is the way (Day 4); today we put it into practice as stewards who serve. Next week we will see how God forms people with different gifts into teams — fellow soldiers in the fivefold ministry, equipping the saints together.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The path of service — Spirit, Word, Life, Reign, God: serving by the Holy Spirit's guidance, according to the truth of Scripture, living out the life of Jesus, letting Jesus reign, and finally giving the glory to God. The goal of our gifts is not that I am seen, but that “to him belong the glory and the dominion.”
q: Who is God? — God has entrusted his varied gifts to people like you. What does that teach you about him?
Who am I? — Are you like a collector who locks gifts away, or a steward who keeps them circulating?
How shall I respond? — Which gift will you use this week to serve a spiritual companion or one of your spiritual children?
lessons.jesus: Jesus prayed to the Father, “I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.” He was the Father's most faithful steward, giving glory to the Father through a lifetime of service and finally laying down even his life.
lessons.pray: Father God, thank you for entrusting your varied gifts to me. I am not the owner but the steward. Help me speak according to your word and serve in your strength, not for my own reputation, but so that in all things you may be glorified through Jesus Christ. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Choose one gift to use this week and write down whom you will serve with it
After completing an act of service, pray silently, “Glory to you”
Invite one of your spiritual children to serve alongside you once
lessons.noon: “As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another.” — Lord, right now I am your faithful steward.

mem.t: He gave some to be apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, shepherds and teachers; for the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving, to the building up of the body of Christ,

lessons.title: The Gift of the Fivefold Ministry
lessons.theme: The ascended Christ gives five kinds of servants to his church

v: But to each one of us, the grace was given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
He gave some to be apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, shepherds and teachers;
for the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving, to the building up of the body of Christ,
until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a full grown man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ,

lessons.still: Quietly call to mind the people who have led you in life: the one who brought you to faith, the one who taught you to read the Bible, the one who shepherded you, the one who pointed you in the right direction. Name them one by one, and give thanks to God for each of them.
teach: A football team has strikers, midfielders, defenders and a goalkeeper. Each has a position, and each sees the game from a different angle: the striker spots the chance to attack, the defender spots the gap at the back. A team made up entirely of strikers would fall apart. What Christ has given his church is likewise a complete line-up.

Verse 7 says that each of us has received grace according to the measure of Christ’s gift. Verse 11 names five kinds of people Christ has given: apostles pioneer and lay foundations; prophets discern and declare the mind of God; evangelists bring people to the Lord; shepherds care for and feed the flock; teachers make the truth plain. Notice the subject of the sentence: “he gave.” These ministries are gifts from the ascended Christ, not titles people compete for.

The fivefold ministry is not five ranks but five perspectives, and no single person can represent the whole Christ alone. A shift in mindset: stop asking “Who is the greatest?” and start asking “Which perspective are we missing?” If our fellowship, small group or ministry team has only one voice, we need to ask the Lord to supply the other gifts.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The “5” in 235 is our fellow soldiers of the fivefold ministry. God’s kingdom system does not rest on one super-leader; it rests on Christ as the Head and the five ministries working together. When we let Jesus reign, ministry does not turn into power; when we let Jesus receive all the glory, ministry does not turn into status.
q: Who is God? — Christ himself gives ministries to the church. What kind of Head does this show you?
Who am I? — Of the five perspectives, which comes most naturally to you? Which is most lacking in you?
How shall I respond? — Which person who has led you will you thank and pray for?
lessons.jesus: Jesus alone holds all five ministries perfectly. He is the Apostle sent by the Father, he is the Prophet, he preached the good news of the kingdom, he is the Good Shepherd, and he is the Teacher his disciples called “Rabbi.” The fivefold ministry of the church exists to display the whole Christ on earth.
lessons.pray: Ascended Lord Jesus, thank you for giving apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds and teachers to your church. Help me to honour every gift and not to mistake my own perspective for the whole picture. Place me where you have appointed me, so that with my fellow soldiers I may build up your body. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write a letter or send a message thanking someone who has shepherded or taught you
Write down which of the five perspectives comes most naturally to you
Pray for your church’s leadership team, naming each person
lessons.noon: “He gave some to be apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, shepherds and teachers” — Lord, thank you right now for giving us grace in its fullness.

lessons.title: Equipping the Saints for Their Work
lessons.theme: Ministry exists not to do everything but to equip the saints

v: Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “The thing that you do is not good.
You will surely wear away, both you, and this people that is with you; for the thing is too heavy for you. You are not able to perform it yourself alone.

from whom all the body, being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part, makes the body increase to the building up of itself in love.

lessons.still: Think of one thing you have always felt is “quicker if I just do it myself.” Quietly lay it before the Lord and ask, “Lord, who do you want me to hand this to, and who do you want me to teach?” Wait a moment, and write down any names that come to mind.
teach: Moses sat alone judging the people from morning till evening, while the queue stood waiting all day long. His father-in-law Jethro put his finger right on it: “The thing that you do is not good.” Not because Moses lacked spirituality or effort, but because he had confused “I can do this” with “I should do this.” The result: he was worn out, and so were the people.

Ephesians 4:12 says the fivefold ministry is “for the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving.” The word translated “perfecting” carries the sense of mending fishing nets or setting broken bones: equipping people and putting them back in their proper place. Verse 16 pictures the outcome: the whole body fitted and knit together, every joint doing its part, each helping the other, and the body growing as it builds itself up in love. A leader’s success is measured not by how much they do themselves, but by how many people they equip.

Doing everything ourselves is often hidden self-rule: we fear others will do it badly, we cannot let go of the feeling of being needed, we want to stay in control. Equipping the saints takes humility, laying down power and returning to our place. A shift in mindset: from “Watch me do it,” to “Let me do it with you,” to “You go and do it, and I’ll support you from behind.” This is exactly the path of multiplication.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Life first, then relationships, then ministry. Equipping is not handing out tasks; it is a life walking alongside a life. Humility draws out humility: when leaders are willing to let go, the saints are willing to take up responsibility. When everyone does their part, God’s kingdom system is built up.
q: Who is God? — God corrected Moses through Jethro’s words. What does this show you about the way he shepherds?
Who am I? — In what area are you “performing it yourself alone,” leaving yourself and others worn out?
How shall I respond? — This week, what one task will you teach one of your spiritual children to do?
lessons.jesus: For three years Jesus walked with the Twelve: first he let them watch, then he had them do it with him, then he sent them out, and when they came back they reviewed it together. In the end he entrusted the Great Commission to these once-weak men. He is the perfect model of equipping the saints.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often do everything myself, because I want control and I want to be needed. Tear down my self-rule and give me a heart to equip others. Teach me to walk alongside, to teach and to let go, so that your body may do its work and grow up in love. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: List one area of service you could hand over to someone else
Spend fifteen minutes showing a brother or sister how to do something, and do it together
Tell a co-worker who is willing to step up, “I believe you can do this.”
lessons.noon: “Being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part” — Lord, right now let me equip others rather than do it all myself.

lessons.title: Working as a Team
lessons.theme: The Holy Spirit speaks in a team that serves the Lord with one heart

v: Now in the assembly that was at Antioch there were some prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”
Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.

lessons.still: Picture yourself sitting in a circle with your co-workers, not for a meeting but to minister to the Lord and wait on him together. Be still for a moment and say to him, “Holy Spirit, please speak among us.”
teach: When geese migrate over long distances they fly in a V formation. When the lead goose tires, it drops back and another takes its place. One goose cannot fly far, but a flock can cross mountains and seas. The work of God’s kingdom is the same: a journey in which a group of people take turns carrying the load and hold one another up.

The leadership team at Antioch was remarkably diverse. Barnabas was a Levite born in Cyprus; Simeon was called Niger (meaning “black”); Lucius came from Cyrene in North Africa; Manaen had grown up with Herod the tetrarch; and Saul had once been a Pharisee who persecuted the church. People of very different backgrounds “served the Lord and fasted” together. And it was in such a team that the Holy Spirit spoke and sent out Barnabas and Saul.

At the heart of teamwork is not a rota of tasks but waiting on the Lord with one heart. God first, then people, then the work: a team worships together first, then decides together. Sending is also the team’s work: those who lay on hands and those who are sent share the burden together. Any small group or ministry team today can become an “Antioch.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: The Holy Spirit is my guide, not some strong personality. Only when everyone on the team lives the self-emptied life can we hear the same voice; only when everyone is humble can we be one amid our differences. That is what fellow soldiers are: not just people who do things together, but people who serve the Lord together.
q: Who is God? — The Holy Spirit spoke while a diverse team was worshipping. What does this show you about how he works?
Who am I? — On a team, do you tend to insist on your own opinion, or can you wait on the Lord with others?
How shall I respond? — Next time your team meets, how much time could you spend worshipping and praying together first?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus sent out his disciples, he sent them “two by two.” He never shaped lone heroes; he built teams who walk together. He himself said that the Son can do nothing of himself, but only what he sees the Father doing.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, make our team minister to the Lord first, and only then do the Lord’s work. Tear down the competition and comparison among us, and let people of different backgrounds and gifts wait on you with one heart. When you speak, we will obey; when you send, we will go together. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Next time your team meets, suggest praying together for ten minutes first
Pray for the co-worker on your team who is most different from you
Ask a co-worker, “How can I support you these days?”
lessons.noon: “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them” — Lord, right now let me hear where you are sending me.

lessons.title: Working Together in Harmony
lessons.theme: The one who plants and the one who waters are the same; we are God’s fellow workers

v: I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase.
So then neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase.
Now he who plants and he who waters are the same, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
For we are God’s fellow workers. You are God’s farming, God’s building.

lessons.still: Think of someone who serves alongside you, and thank the Lord for them: “Lord, thank you for giving me this co-worker. They can do what I cannot.” Let gratitude take the place of comparison.
teach: In a symphony the violins carry the melody, the cellos hold down the bass, and the timpani sound only now and then. If every player insisted on playing the melody, all you would have is noise. True teamwork means knowing when to play and when to rest, when to stand in front and when to hold others up from behind.

The Corinthians said, “I follow Paul,” and “I follow Apollos,” turning co-workers into factions. But Paul said: I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase; the one who plants and the one who waters are the same. The secret of working together lies in verse 9: we are “God’s fellow workers.” When the focus shifts from “Who gets the credit?” to “What is God doing?”, co-workers no longer need to compare themselves with one another.

Working together means accepting different rhythms. Pioneers move fast; shepherds move steadily. Prophetic people speak bluntly; pastoral people are considerate. Different does not mean right or wrong; it means complementary. Partnership begins when I appreciate other people’s gifts instead of trying to remake them in my image. Each will receive a reward according to their own labour, so there is no need to grab someone else’s.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility draws out humility, and both sides win. The key to working together is focus: when our focus is on Jesus, co-workers are comrades; when our focus is on ourselves, co-workers become rivals. When the glory goes to God, there is no need to fight over credit.
q: Who is God? — “God who gives the increase.” How does this shape the way you see the fruit of your service?
Who am I? — Have you ever quietly compared yourself with a co-worker, or tried to make someone more like you?
How shall I respond? — How will you concretely show appreciation to a co-worker who is very different from you?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said that the one who reaps gathers fruit to eternal life, “that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together.” He values the one who sows as much as the one who reaps. In his eyes, others laboured and we reap, and it is all part of one harvest.
lessons.pray: Lord, we are your fellow workers. Remove from my heart every thought of comparison and competing for credit. Make me glad to plant and glad to water, glad to stand in front and glad to stand behind. Let all the growth be credited to you and all the glory be given to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Tell a co-worker face to face that you value a gift in them that you do not have
In one area of service, deliberately take a supporting role so that someone else can flourish
Pray a blessing over a co-worker you have disagreed with
lessons.noon: “For we are God’s fellow workers” — Lord, right now let me work with one heart, with you and with my brothers and sisters.

lessons.title: Building Up the Body of Christ
lessons.theme: We are all living stones, built together into a dwelling place for God

v: Come to him, a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen by God, precious.
You also as living stones are built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
in whom you also are built together for a habitation of God in the Spirit.

lessons.still: Imagine you are a stone, picked up by the Lord’s hand, shaped and set into a wall, pressed close against the stones beside you. Quietly say, “Lord, put me in the place you want me.”
teach: Stones scattered on the ground are just stones, however fine the material. Only when a builder lays them one by one, each bearing weight and supporting the others, do they become a house. However beautiful a single stone may be, no one can live in it. God wants not just a lot of good Christians, but a spiritual home.

Peter calls the Lord “a living stone,” rejected by people yet chosen by God and precious. As we come to him, we too become living stones, built up into a spiritual house. Paul says we are “built together” into a dwelling place for God in the Spirit. The word “together” is the key: God’s dwelling is not found in one person, but among many people joined to one another.

This week we have seen the fivefold ministry (Day 1), equipping the saints (Day 2), working as a team (Day 3) and working together in harmony (Day 4). Today we see the goal: building up the body of Christ. Next week we face a fact: everyone who builds God’s house will meet spiritual attack, and so we must put on the full armour God provides.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One purpose: to build what belongs to God, God’s kingdom system. That system is not an organisational chart; it is a spiritual house with Christ as the cornerstone and all the saints as living stones. When we let Jesus reign, this house belongs to God; when we let Jesus receive all the glory, this house is filled with God’s presence.
q: Who is God? — The stone people rejected became God’s precious living stone. What kind of Lord does this show you?
Who am I? — Are you a stone sitting off by yourself, or a living stone willing to be built into the wall?
How shall I respond? — With which fellow soldiers will you share the responsibility of building?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “On this rock I will build my assembly.” He is the builder, and he is also the cornerstone. We do not build the church for Jesus; we are built by him and work alongside him. He is still building today, until his bride is made ready.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you are the living stone and the cornerstone. I come to you willing to be shaped and built by you. Join me together with my fellow soldiers, so that we become a dwelling place of God in the Spirit, and let your house be filled with your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the names of three fellow soldiers and pray for them
Meet with a co-worker and share your gifts and burdens with each other
At a gathering this week, take the initiative on one small task that builds others up
lessons.noon: “In whom you also are built together for a habitation of God in the Spirit.” — Lord, right now build me into your house.

mem.t: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might. Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.

lessons.title: The Nature of the Battle
lessons.theme: Our real enemy is not people but the powers of darkness

v: For our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against the principalities, against the powers, against the world’s rulers of the darkness of this age, and against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places.
for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty before God to the throwing down of strongholds,
throwing down imaginations and every high thing that is exalted against the knowledge of God and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ,

lessons.still: Think of someone who has recently made you angry or hurt you. Softly say before the Lord, “Lord, this person is not my enemy.” Hand your anger toward them over to the Lord, and then turn your eyes to the real battle.
teach: For soldiers fighting in thick fog, the greatest danger is not the enemy but hitting their own side. So it is with many conflicts in families, churches and ministry teams: we take aim at the people next to us and fail to see the real enemy behind them.

Paul says our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, powers and the world rulers of this darkness. Where is the battlefield? 2 Corinthians 10 tells us: “strongholds,” “every high thing,” “every thought.” Satan’s main attack is to build, inside people’s minds, high walls that keep them from knowing God. Our weapons are for “bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ.”

So the first shift in mindset for spiritual warfare is this: people are not my enemies; people need to be won back. The second is this: the battlefield is the mind, not only our circumstances. Ever since Eden, Satan has attacked with the lie, “You will be like God.” Every thought that makes me want to be my own king is a stronghold that must be torn down.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-emptied life overcomes Satan. Satan’s very nature is pride; he wants people to leave their place. Our victory is to return to our place and let Jesus reign. We do not fight against people but against pride; we do not rely on the flesh but on the Holy Spirit. Our focus is on Jesus, not on people and not on circumstances.
q: Who is God? — God gives weapons that are “mighty before God.” What does this show you about him?
Who am I? — Whom have you recently been treating as an enemy?
How shall I respond? — What “stronghold” in your heart needs to be taken captive and brought into obedience to Christ?
lessons.jesus: When Peter urged Jesus not to take the way of the cross, Jesus said, “Get behind me, Satan!” He did not treat Peter as an enemy, but he discerned the voice behind Peter’s words. He loved Peter, and at the same time rejected the temptation of thinking “not the things of God, but the things of men.”
lessons.pray: Lord, open my eyes to see the real battle. I will no longer treat people as enemies or fight with the weapons of the flesh. Tear down the proud strongholds in my heart, take my thoughts captive, and bring me into complete obedience to Christ. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Pray a blessing, not an accusation, over someone you are in conflict with
Write down a lie that often attacks you, and find a verse to counter it
Whenever you feel angry today, silently say, “This person is not my enemy.”
lessons.noon: “Throwing down imaginations and every high thing that is exalted against the knowledge of God and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ” — Lord, right now my thoughts belong to you.

lessons.title: The Whole Armour
lessons.theme: To put on God’s armour is to put on Christ himself

v: Stand therefore, having the utility belt of truth buckled around your waist, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness,
and having fitted your feet with the preparation of the Good News of peace,
above all, taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the fiery darts of the evil one.
And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God;

lessons.still: Stand up and lightly touch, in turn, your waist, your chest, your feet, your arm and your head. With each touch, silently name a piece of armour: truth, righteousness, peace, faith, salvation. Finally, picture yourself gripping God’s word. Say to the Lord, “I put you on.”
teach: A soldier going into battle does not wear just one piece of armour. Without a helmet, even the best breastplate cannot save his life; with a sword but no boots, he cannot keep his footing. When Paul wrote this letter he was a prisoner for the Lord, and he knew the equipment of Roman soldiers intimately. Through this picture the Holy Spirit teaches us that spiritual protection must be “whole.”

Each piece of armour has its purpose. The belt of truth keeps lies from loosening us; the breastplate of righteousness guards the conscience; the shoes of the gospel of peace give us sure footing, ready at any time to share the good news; the shield of faith quenches the fiery arrows of the evil one; the helmet of salvation guards our thinking; the sword of the Spirit, the word of God, is our weapon of attack. These are not merely techniques. They point to Christ himself: he is the truth, our righteousness, our peace and our salvation.

So putting on the armour really means “putting on the Lord Jesus Christ” every day (Romans 13:14). It is not enough to recite a formula once in the morning. Every time a temptation, a lie or a fear comes at us, we return to Christ. The whole armour does not make me stronger; it hides me more deeply in the Lord.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Scripture is my standard: the sword of the Spirit is the word of God. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he teaches me when to raise the shield. Jesus is my example: he overcame in the wilderness with “It is written.” These three foundations are our armour for every day.
q: Who is God? — God himself supplies the whole armour. What kind of Commander does this show you?
Who am I? — Which piece of armour do you most often forget to put on?
How shall I respond? — Which verse will you memorise today to be the sword in your hand?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was tempted in the wilderness, all three of his answers began, “It is written.” He did not prove himself with a miracle, and he did not debate with the devil; he simply stood firm on the word of God. He himself showed us how to take up the sword of the Spirit.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you are my truth, my righteousness, my peace and my salvation. Today I put you on, and I take up the shield of faith and the word of God. Holy Spirit, remind me to stand in Christ whenever an attack comes. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: In the morning, take one minute to “put on” each piece of armour in prayer
Memorise a verse that confronts your greatest weakness
When temptation comes, say that verse, silently or aloud
lessons.noon: “And the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God” — Lord, right now I stand firm on your word.

lessons.title: Strong in the Lord
lessons.theme: The battle belongs to the Lord, not to me

v: and that all this assembly may know that the LORD doesn’t save with sword and spear; for the battle is the LORD’s, and he will give you into our hand.”
He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, and in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then am I strong.

lessons.still: Name a “giant” that frightens you: a difficulty, a weakness, a situation with no end in sight. Call it by name, then say, “Lord, you are bigger than this.” Quietly trust him.
teach: When the shepherd boy David was about to face the towering Goliath, Saul dressed him in his own armour. But David was not used to it and took it off, going out with only his staff, five smooth stones and his sling. He relied not on better equipment but on a deeper knowledge: this battle belonged to the Lord.

David said, “The battle is Yahweh’s.” Paul heard the Lord say, “My power is made perfect in weakness.” Both passages point to the same truth: strength is not puffing ourselves up but relying on the Lord’s mighty power. Paul even says, “When I am weak, then am I strong.” Admitting our weakness becomes the very doorway through which Christ’s power comes to rest on us.

This week’s memory verse says, “Be strong in the Lord, and in the strength of his might.” In spiritual warfare the most dangerous people are not the weak but those who think they are strong. They put on Saul’s armour and fight their own way. Live from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself. Relying on ourselves brings worry; relying on the Lord brings victory.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility is laying down power and returning to our place. Admitting “I can’t” is our place as human beings; declaring “The Lord can” is letting God be God. The proud rely on their own armour; the humble rely on the name of the Lord. This is how humility overcomes pride and the self-emptied life overcomes Satan.
q: Who is God? — “My grace is sufficient for you.” Where have you recently experienced these words?
Who am I? — Are you still wearing “Saul’s armour,” fighting your own way?
How shall I respond? — Which weakness will you confess to the Lord today, so that his power may rest on you?
lessons.jesus: On the cross Jesus looked weakest of all: nailed, mocked, forsaken. Yet it was there that he disarmed the principalities and powers and triumphed over them by the cross. God’s power was made perfect in the utter weakness of the cross.
lessons.pray: Lord, I admit that I am weak, and I admit that I often try to be strong in myself. Today I take off my own armour and rely on your name alone. Your grace is sufficient for me. Let your power be made perfect in my weakness, for the battle belongs to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down your current “giant,” and next to it write, “The battle is the Lord’s”
Confess one weakness to a spiritual companion and ask them to pray for you
Before each difficult task today, pray, “Lord, I rely on you.”
lessons.noon: “My grace is sufficient for you” — Lord, right now in my weakness I rely on your mighty power.

lessons.title: Prayer Is Warfare
lessons.theme: Prayer is an unseen battlefield, and a battlefield we share as a team

v: with all prayer and requests, praying at all times in the Spirit, and being watchful to this end in all perseverance and requests for all the saints.
When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed. When he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

But Moses’ hands were heavy; so they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His hands were steady until sunset.

lessons.still: Raise both hands for one minute and feel your arms slowly grow heavy. Think of Moses, and think of those who have prayed for you. Say to the Lord, “Lord, I need someone to hold up my hands, and I am willing to hold up the hands of others.”
teach: On a battlefield, the soldiers at the front can see the enemy; the signallers in the rear cannot. Yet if communications are cut, the front line is left stranded. Prayer is the communication line of spiritual warfare, linking the battlefield to the Commander. It looks unremarkable, yet victory or defeat depends on it.

Right after listing the whole armour, Ephesians says, “praying at all times in the Spirit, with all prayer and requests.” Prayer is not just one more piece of equipment; it is how we wear the armour and go into battle. Exodus 17 makes it concrete: Joshua fought in the valley while Moses raised his hands on the hill. When Moses raised his hands, Israel prevailed. When his hands grew heavy, Aaron and Hur held them up, one on each side, until sunset.

This is a picture of team prayer: some are on the front line, some are on the hill, and some hold up the hands of the one who prays. No one can keep their hands raised forever. This is what fellow soldiers are for: when the other person’s hands grow heavy, you hold them up, one on each side. Three weeks ago we learned about praying with one heart; today we see that praying with one heart is fighting with one heart.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The fellow soldiers in 235 do not only work together in ministry; they share the load in prayer. Prayer is an act of letting Jesus reign: it admits that victory is not in my hands but in God’s. To pray the Lord’s Prayer to its fulfilment is to give the kingdom, the power and the glory back to God.
q: Who is God? — Why did God link the victory to Moses’ raised hands in prayer?
Who am I? — Are you Moses raising his hands, Aaron and Hur holding them up, or someone who usually fights alone?
How shall I respond? — Whose hands among your fellow soldiers will you hold up this week?
lessons.jesus: In Gethsemane, in deep anguish, Jesus prayed all the more earnestly, and his sweat fell to the ground like great drops of blood. He took three disciples with him and asked them to keep watch and pray. The victory of the cross was first settled in prayer.
lessons.pray: Lord, teach me to treat prayer as warfare, not routine. Help me to pray at all times in the Spirit, with all kinds of prayers, and for all the saints. Give me a heart to support others, so that when a fellow soldier’s hands grow heavy, I will hold them up until victory comes. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Ask a fellow soldier, “What can I pray for you?”
Spend fifteen focused minutes praying for a co-worker serving on the front line
Set a reminder to pray for all the saints for one minute at the same time every day
lessons.noon: “Praying at all times in the Spirit” — Lord, right now I lift up my hands to you.

lessons.title: Standing Firm
lessons.theme: Resist the devil; overcome by the blood of the Lamb and our testimony

v: Be sober and self-controlled. Be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
Withstand him steadfast in your faith, knowing that your brothers who are in the world are undergoing the same sufferings.
They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony. They didn’t love their life, even to death.

lessons.still: Plant both feet flat on the floor and feel how solid the ground is beneath you. Say to the Lord, “Lord, I stand on your word and in your precious blood.” Take three deep breaths, and with each one declare in your heart, “I stand firm.”
teach: After a typhoon, the trees uprooted along the shore are often the ones with lush foliage but shallow roots. Old trees that have weathered many storms may be bent, but they have not fallen. Spiritual victory does not always mean routing the enemy; it means still “standing” in the storm.

Peter describes the devil as a roaring lion prowling around, looking for someone to devour, and lions go after the stragglers and the careless. The response is to be sober, to be watchful, to resist him firm in the faith, and to know that “your brothers in the world are undergoing the same sufferings”: you are not alone. Revelation 12:11 reveals the secret of victory: the blood of the Lamb, the word of our testimony, and not loving our lives.

This week we have seen the nature of the battle (Day 1), the whole armour (Day 2), being strong in the Lord (Day 3) and prayer as warfare (Day 4). Today it is standing firm. We stand not because we are strong but because the Lamb has already won. Next week we move to another front line, money, and ask who is reigning in our wallets.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-emptied life overcomes Satan, and “they didn’t love their life” is the self-emptied life at its fullest. Satan can accuse those who live a self-ruled life, but he cannot defeat someone who is wholly hidden in the blood of the Lamb and lives for the Lord. Our focus is not the lion’s roar but the Lamb who has already won.
q: Who is God? — The blood of the Lamb has already overcome the accuser. How does this change the way you see Satan’s attacks?
Who am I? — Are you currently isolated or careless?
How shall I respond? — With whom will you share a “word of your testimony”?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said to Peter, “But I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn’t fail.” He knew Peter would fall, yet he prayed for him beforehand and restored him after the resurrection. We can stand firm because our High Priest always lives to intercede for us.
lessons.pray: Victorious Lamb, I stand in your precious blood and will no longer be shaken by the voice of the accuser. Make me sober and watchful, resisting the devil firm in the faith. I do not cling to my own life; I only long for you to be glorified in me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down a testimony of God’s victory that you have personally experienced
Agree with a spiritual companion to check in on and watch over each other this week
Before sleep, declare, “I overcome by the blood of the Lamb.”
lessons.noon: “They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony” — Lord, right now I stand in your victory.
