mem.t: Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in my house, and test me now in this,” says the LORD of Armies, “if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there will not be enough room for.

lessons.title: Everything Belongs to God
lessons.theme: I am not an owner but a steward of God’s resources

v: The earth is the LORD’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it.
But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and we have given you of your own.

lessons.still: Look at the things around you: your phone, your wallet, the table and chairs, your clothes. One by one, say to the Lord, “This is yours.” Finally, place your hand on your chest and quietly say, “And I am yours too.”
teach: A hotel guest may use everything in the room: the bed, the lamps, the towels, the air conditioning. Yet no one thinks the towels belong to them; at checkout everything is handed back as it was. So it is with us in this world: nothing we use is truly ours. It has all been entrusted to us for a while.

Psalm 24:1 declares that the earth and everything in it belong to the Lord. When David gave toward building the temple, the people gladly offered great amounts of gold and silver, yet David said, “Who am I … we have given you of your own.” Giving is not handing God something of ours; it is giving back to God what is his. The real question is not “How much should I give to God?” but “How much should I keep for myself?”

Once our mindset changes, money weighs differently: from “my money” to “the Lord’s money,” from “what I earned” to “what he gave,” from the temporary to the eternal. Money is the most honest test of who is reigning. We can sing “The Lord is my King” at church, but our bank statements tell the truth.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Letting Jesus reign must include our wallets. The self-ruled life says, “This is mine”; the self-emptied life says, “This is the Lord’s.” Pride is grasping power, and money is the easiest power to grasp. Handing ownership back to God is returning to our place as stewards.
q: Who is God? — “All things come from you.” What does this show you about God?
Who am I? — Right now, do you relate to money more like an owner or a steward?
How shall I respond? — Over which possession will you concretely hand ownership back to the Lord?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “Give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” Caesar’s image was on the coin, but God’s image is on us. God wants not only our money but our whole selves, the people who bear his image.
lessons.pray: Lord, the earth and everything in it are yours, and I am yours too. I confess that I often treat what you have entrusted to me as my own property. Today I hand ownership back to you. Be Lord of my wallet, and make me a faithful steward. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write “This is the Lord’s” on or beside your wallet or payment app
Review last month’s spending and see where the money went
Pray over one possession you have been clinging to, and entrust it to God
lessons.noon: “And we have given you of your own.” — Lord, right now all that I have is yours.

lessons.title: The Tithe
lessons.theme: Tithing is a lesson in faith, not a transaction to buy blessing

v: Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in my house, and test me now in this,” says the LORD of Armies, “if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there will not be enough room for.

“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. But you ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.

lessons.still: Quietly ask yourself, “Do I really believe God will provide for me?” There is no need to rush an answer. Let the Holy Spirit shine on your fears and your sources of security where money is concerned, and lay them openly before the Lord.
teach: A farmer keeps back his best bag of seed to sow in the field rather than grinding it into flour. Others see one less bag of grain; the farmer sees faith in the coming harvest. The tithe is like that: not a loss, but faith sown into God’s storehouse.

In Malachi’s day the people were robbing God of the tithe they owed, yet God invited them: “Test me now in this.” It is one of the rare places in Scripture where God himself invites people to put him to the test. Jesus also said tithing should “not be left undone,” yet he rebuked the Pharisees even more for neglecting “justice, mercy, and faith.” The tithe is not the finishing line but the starting line; not a legal calculation but an expression of love and trust.

Beware of two errors. One treats the tithe as an investment to buy blessing: “I give God ten, so God owes me a hundred.” That is prosperity theology. The other uses grace as an excuse to give nothing at all. Grace comes first: we do not give to earn blessing; we give because we have already been blessed. The tithe is a concrete practice of “letting God be God” with our money.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Of the eight steps for changing our mindset, Practice and Review are nowhere more visible than with money. Tithing is a practical act of letting Jesus reign, and it also supplies what builds God’s kingdom system, so that there is food in God’s house and the work of the kingdom can move forward.
q: Who is God? — God says, “Test me now in this.” What does this show you about his faithfulness?
Who am I? — In giving, are you more prone to the error of “buying blessing” or of “not giving”?
How shall I respond? — What step of faith are you willing to take in your giving?
lessons.jesus: Jesus never avoided talking about money, but he always saw the heart behind it. When Zacchaeus gave half his possessions to the poor, Jesus said, “Today, salvation has come to this house.” The turning of his money bore witness to the turning of his heart.
lessons.pray: Faithful Father, you say, “Test me now in this,” and I want to answer you in faith. Take away my fear of not having enough, and take away any desire to trade my giving for blessing. I give because I have already been blessed; I offer because you are my King. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Honestly work out what proportion of your income you currently give
Before you next give, pray first and set the amount in faith
As you give, pray silently, “Lord, I give because I have already been blessed.”
lessons.noon: “And test me now in this,” says the LORD of Armies, “if I will not open you the windows of heaven” — Lord, right now I trust in your provision.

lessons.title: The Widow’s Two Small Coins
lessons.theme: God looks not at the amount but at the heart and the cost

v: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much.
A poor widow came and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin.
He called his disciples to himself and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,
for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”

lessons.still: Imagine Jesus sitting opposite the treasury, watching you. His gaze is not one of judgement but of tenderness. Quietly say to the Lord, “Lord, you see what I offer, and you see my heart.”
teach: A child spends their pocket money on a single flower for their mother. It wilts in a few days and cost very little, yet the mother presses it in a book and treasures it for years, because that flower carries the child’s whole heart. In love, value is never measured by the price tag.

Jesus “sat down opposite the treasury, and saw how the multitude cast money” in. He was watching how, not just how much. The rich put in large amounts; the widow put in only two small coins. Yet Jesus’ verdict turns everything upside down: “This poor widow gave more than all those who are giving.” For the rich gave out of their abundance, but she gave out of her poverty, all she had to live on.

God does not measure how much you give but how much you keep, and what it costs you. This comforts the poor: a small gift is not small in God’s eyes. It also challenges the well-off: a large sum is not necessarily a large offering. The widow entrusted her whole self to God; her two small coins were an act of total trust in him.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The widow’s gift was a self-emptied gift: not given to be seen, with no fallback, relying wholly on God. Her focus was on God, not on what others thought. A shift in perspective: from human eyes to God’s eyes, from the outward amount to the inward heart.
q: Who is God? — Jesus “sat down opposite the treasury” and watched closely. What does this show you about him?
Who am I? — Do you mostly give out of “abundance,” or have you ever given out of “poverty”?
How shall I respond? — What “two small coins” could you offer wholeheartedly to the Lord today?
lessons.jesus: Not long after speaking about the widow, Jesus himself gave everything, not just what he had to live on but his very life. The widow put in two small coins; Jesus put in himself. He is the most complete giver of all.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for seeing the offerings no one notices. I will no longer compare amounts; I only want to give you my true heart. Teach me the widow’s trust and your own self-giving, so that I place all I have in your hands. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Make an offering that costs you something, whatever the amount
Quietly help a brother or sister in financial difficulty, without letting anyone know
Thank God for someone you know who gives sacrificially without being noticed
lessons.noon: “This poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury” — Lord, right now I offer you my true heart.

lessons.title: A Cheerful Giver
lessons.theme: God loves a cheerful giver

v: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that you through his poverty might become rich.
Remember this: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. He who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
And God is able to make all grace abound to you, that you, always having all sufficiency in everything, may abound to every good work.

lessons.still: Remember the joy you felt when you gave a gift to someone you love. Bring that feeling before the Lord and quietly say, “Lord, may I feel that same joy when I give to you and to others.”
teach: A fountain stays fresh because water keeps flowing in and keeps flowing out. The Dead Sea is dead because water only flows in and never out. If money only ever comes in and never goes out, the heart slowly grows heavy and dry. Cheerful giving keeps life flowing.

The churches of Macedonia, in deep poverty, overflowed in rich generosity. Paul points to the source: the Lord Jesus was rich, yet for our sake he became poor. The motivation for giving is not command but grace. So Paul says, “not grudgingly or under compulsion,” because “God loves a cheerful giver.” God looks not only at what we give but at how we give.

“He who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly” is not a formula for return on investment but a spiritual principle: generous people experience more of God’s grace, so that they have “all sufficiency in everything” and “abound to every good work.” God gives to us so that we can give again. A shift in mindset: from “protecting what’s mine” to “circulating what is God’s.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: Let Jesus receive all the glory. Cheerful giving is an act of thankful worship. The final step on the path of service is “God”: giving glory to God and giving thanks in everything. Reluctant giving is the calculation of the self-ruled life; cheerful giving is the overflow of the self-emptied life.
q: Who is God? — “Though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor.” What does this show you about Christ?
Who am I? — Is your giving mostly cheerful, or grudging and under compulsion?
How shall I respond? — How could you cheerfully bless someone this week?
lessons.jesus: Paul quotes the Lord Jesus: “It is more blessed to give than to receive.” This sums up Jesus’ whole life: he gave healing, he gave his time, he gave forgiveness, and in the end he gave his life. His giving was never forced, for he gave willingly and gladly.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you were rich, yet for my sake you became poor, and your grace has made me rich. Put a cheerful heart within me, so that I give neither grudgingly nor under compulsion. Like a fountain, let your grace flow out through me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Plan one act of cheerful giving this week, and pray over it with joy
Buy a brother or sister a coffee and sincerely ask how they are doing
Write down three ways the Lord has made you “rich”
lessons.noon: “God loves a cheerful giver” — Lord, right now let your grace flow out through me.

lessons.title: Treasure in Heaven
lessons.theme: Store up treasure in heaven, for where your treasure is, there your heart will be

v: “Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;
but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal;
for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
Charge those who are rich in this present age that they not be arrogant, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on the living God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy;

lessons.still: Imagine yourself standing at the end of your life, looking back. Which things will be left behind on earth? Which will be carried into eternity? Be still for a while, and let the Lord rearrange the order of values in your heart.
teach: People emigrating to another country do not leave all their assets in the place they are leaving; they transfer their resources to the country where they are going. We are citizens of heaven, and earth is only where we are staying for a while. We cannot take our earthly wealth with us, but we can “transfer” our treasure to heaven ahead of time.

Jesus names three dangers for earthly treasure: moth, rust and thieves, natural decay and human theft. Treasure in heaven, however, is never lost. Verse 21 gets to the heart of it: where your treasure is, there your heart will be. Money not only reveals the direction of the heart; it pulls the heart in that direction. Paul likewise charges the rich not to put their hope in uncertain riches but in God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy.

This week we have moved from everything belongs to God (Day 1), the tithe (Day 2), the widow’s heart (Day 3) and the cheerful giver (Day 4) to today’s treasure in heaven. Investing money in people’s eternal lives is storing up treasure in heaven. Next week we will see another precious treasure of God’s kingdom: the unity of brothers and sisters.
lessons.light: 321 Light: A shift in perspective: from earthly to heavenly, from temporary to eternal. People matter more than tasks, and relationships matter more than things. Using money to build people up, to equip them and to share the gospel is transferring treasure to heaven and building God’s kingdom system.
q: Who is God? — God “richly provides us with everything to enjoy.” What does this show you about him?
Who am I? — Looking at your spending, where is your heart right now?
How shall I respond? — This week, which of your resources could you invest in someone’s eternal life?
lessons.jesus: Jesus stored up no treasure on earth; he said, “the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.” Yet he was the richest of all, because his treasure was the Father’s delight and the souls of people. He gave up everything to redeem us; we are his treasure.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, take away my heart’s reliance on money. Everything on earth will pass away; only you and your kingdom remain for ever. Teach me to store up treasure in heaven and to invest my resources in people’s lives, so that my heart follows hard after you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Set aside an amount in this month’s budget specifically for evangelism or care
Sort out something you no longer need and give it to someone who needs it
Share with your family or a spiritual companion: “Where is my treasure?”
lessons.noon: “For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” — Lord, right now my heart is with you.

mem.t: that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that you sent me.

lessons.title: Jesus’ Prayer for Unity
lessons.theme: On the eve of the cross, Jesus prayed for our unity

v: “Not for these only do I pray, but for those also who will believe in me through their word,
that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that you sent me.
The glory which you have given me, I have given to them, that they may be one, even as we are one,
I in them, and you in me, that they may be perfected into one, that the world may know that you sent me and loved them, even as you loved me.

lessons.still: Imagine yourself sitting in the room of the Last Supper, listening to Jesus pray. He mentions “those who will believe in me through their word.” That means you. Quietly let the wonder of being remembered by the Lord fill you.
teach: What a person says just before parting often reveals what matters to them most. On the night he was betrayed, Jesus’ last long prayer was not mostly for himself. He prayed for his disciples, and for believers in every age, that they would “be one.” Unity was among the deepest burdens on Jesus’ heart.

Jesus’ prayer for unity has three layers. The source of unity is the triune God: “even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you.” The place of unity is in God: “that they also may be one in us.” The purpose of unity is gospel witness: “that the world may believe that you sent me.” Unity is not just an internal church matter; it is the way the world comes to know Jesus.

So division in the church is not only an internal problem; it is an obstacle to the gospel. When the world sees Christians loving one another, it sees God; when it sees Christians attacking one another, it cannot see God. A shift in mindset: unity is not an optional virtue but part of the Great Commission.
lessons.light: 321 Light: God’s kingdom system takes the unity of the triune God as its blueprint. When we let Jesus reign, he becomes the centre among us; when we let Jesus receive all the glory, we stop fighting for our own names. Unity is not something we manufacture; it is something we receive in God.
q: Who is God? — What kind of God do you see in the unity between the Father and the Son?
Who am I? — Jesus prayed for you that night too. How does that make you feel?
How shall I respond? — In your life, which broken relationship is standing in the way of the gospel?
lessons.jesus: Jesus did not only pray for unity; he died for it. On the cross he broke down the dividing wall, making Jews and Gentiles one new humanity in himself. Our unity was bought with his precious blood.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for praying for me on the night you were betrayed. Make us one, as you and the Father are one, so that the world may see from our love for one another that the Father sent you. And begin with me: help me mend the cracks where I am. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Pray John 17:21 over your church or fellowship
Pray a blessing over another church or fellowship
Reach out to a brother or sister you have not been in touch with for a long time
lessons.noon: “That they may all be one” — Lord, right now make my heart one with yours.

lessons.title: Self-Rule Breeds Conflict
lessons.theme: The root of conflict is not in others but in the desires within me

v: Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members?
for you are still fleshly. For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions among you, aren’t you fleshly, and don’t you walk in the ways of men?
For when one says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” aren’t you fleshly?

lessons.still: Recall your most recent argument. For now, set aside where the other person went wrong, and simply ask the Lord, “In that situation, what was I wanting to get?” Let the Holy Spirit shine on your own desires behind the conflict.
teach: Two hedgehogs on a freezing winter night want to keep each other warm. If they get too close, they prick each other; if they stay too far apart, they are cold. People are often like that. The problem is not closeness but the spines. If the spines are not dealt with, the closer the relationship, the deeper the wounds.

James asks bluntly: where do the fights and quarrels among you come from? The answer is not “because he went too far,” but “from your pleasures that war in your members.” Paul likewise says the jealousy and strife among the Corinthians showed they were “still fleshly.” Some said, “I follow Paul,” others, “I follow Apollos”; even spiritual leaders had become tools for comparison and taking sides.

The root of conflict is self-rule: I want it my way, I want to be valued, I want to win. Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose. In a conflict, the most honest question is not “Who is right and who is wrong?” but “Who is reigning right now?” When I own up to my own desires, I truly open the door to unity.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Self-rule is the root of the fall and the root of conflict. If our focus is on others, we see only the spines on them; when our focus returns to Jesus, we see the spines on ourselves. A shift in mindset: from “It’s all their problem” to “Lord, change me first.”
q: Who is God? — Why does God go straight to the desires of the heart rather than dealing first with circumstances?
Who am I? — In your most recent conflict, what did you really want?
How shall I respond? — To whom will you admit your self-rule in a conflict?
lessons.jesus: At the Last Supper the disciples were still arguing about who was the greatest. Jesus did not join the debate. He got up, wrapped a towel around his waist and washed their feet. He answered their self-ruled quarrel with a self-emptied act.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that conflict often springs from the desires within me: wanting to be valued, wanting to win, wanting things my way. Pull out my spines, and help me see myself first in every conflict. Today I give up the throne to you. Please reign. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down what you really wanted in your most recent conflict
Go to the other person in that conflict and admit your part first
When you want to argue, pause for ten seconds and silently ask, “Who is reigning?”
lessons.noon: “Where do wars and fightings among you come from?” — Lord, right now search me first.

lessons.title: Eager to Keep Unity
lessons.theme: Unity is given by the Spirit, and we must work hard to keep it

v: I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,
with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
There is one body and one Spirit, even as you also were called in one hope of your calling,

lessons.still: Slowly say four words: humility, gentleness, patience, forbearance. After each one, pause and think of someone who needs you to treat them that way, and place them in the Lord’s hands.
teach: A precious porcelain heirloom does not stay intact for ever just because you own it. It needs to be placed with care, dusted regularly, and carefully wrapped when you move house. Unity is the same: it is a treasure God gives, and if we do not cherish and guard it, a single knock can crack it.

Paul speaks of keeping unity, not creating it. Unity is “of the Spirit”; we cannot manufacture it, only keep it. “Being eager” means it takes effort and cost. How do we keep it? Verses 2–3 list the ways: lowliness, humility, patience, bearing with one another in love, and the bond of peace. Verse 4 reminds us: there is one body and one Spirit.

Unity is not uniformity. It does not mean everyone thinks and acts the same, but that we keep one heart amid our differences, like different notes sounding together to make a beautiful chord. Keeping unity often means giving way on non-essentials, standing firm on essential truth, and holding on to love in all things.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Here the fruit of 920 is borne: humility, gentleness, patience, love and peace are all fruit of the Spirit. Keeping unity does not depend on technique but on a self-emptied life. People matter more than tasks: do not let who is right about one issue destroy the unity the Spirit has given.
q: Who is God? — The Holy Spirit gives unity as a gift. What does this show you about him?
Who am I? — Of humility, gentleness, patience and forbearance, which do you lack most?
How shall I respond? — On which non-essential matter do you need to give way for the sake of unity?
lessons.jesus: Among Jesus’ disciples were Simon the Zealot and Matthew the tax collector, one who hated Rome and one who collected taxes for Rome. Yet Jesus put them on the same team. In him, people on opposite sides learned to bear with one another.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, thank you for the gift of unity. Make me humble, gentle and patient in all things, bearing with others in love and bound to them in peace. I am willing to give way in small things; make me stand firm in the truth, and help me hold on to love in everything. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Give way on one non-essential matter, and do it with joy
Say a word of appreciation to someone whose personality is very different from yours
Before you speak today, ask yourself: will this build connection or tear down?
lessons.noon: “Being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” — Lord, right now make me a messenger of unity.

lessons.title: Humility Draws Out Humility
lessons.theme: Counting others better than ourselves opens the door to unity

v: make my joy full by being like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;
doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.

lessons.still: Think of someone you often secretly feel you are better than. Before the Lord, honestly count three ways in which they are better than you, and let this exercise slowly soften your heart.
teach: Two cars meet in a narrow lane. Neither will back up, so neither can get through. If just one of them reverses a few metres, both can pass. Humility looks like losing out, but in fact it lets both sides move forward. Pride provokes pride; humility draws out humility.

Paul urges the Philippian church to be “like-minded, having the same love,” and his method is very concrete: do nothing out of rivalry or conceit, but in humility “each counting others better than himself,” “not just looking to his own things, but … also to the things of others.” This is not putting ourselves down; it is choosing to see God’s grace in others and to take their needs to heart.

In the Philippian church two sisters, Euodia and Syntyche, needed to be reconciled (4:2). Paul did not rule on who was right. He brought them before the heart of Christ. Unity often begins when one side humbles itself first. Do not wait for the other person to change first. Humble people take the initiative to reverse, to apologise and to bless, and so they open the way for both sides to win.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility is the key to revival, and the key to unity. Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility draws out humility, and both sides win. When we lay down power and return to our place, letting people be people and letting God be God, relationships are healed.
q: Who is God? — What does Christ’s self-emptying heart show you about how God treats people?
Who am I? — Do you often wait for others to give way or apologise first?
How shall I respond? — In which relationship will you be the first to “reverse” today?
lessons.jesus: Though Jesus existed in the form of God, he emptied himself and became a servant. He did not wait for others to humble themselves first; he humbled himself first, all the way down to the cross. This Lord who humbled himself first has drawn countless people into humility and reconciliation.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you humbled yourself first, you lowered yourself first, you gave yourself first. Help me stop waiting for others to change first. Instead, let me be humble first, count others better than myself, and look to their interests too. Let my humility draw out humility, so that your body wins together. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three ways in which someone you often compare yourself with is better than you
Take the first step towards healing a relationship that is stuck
At least once today, put someone else’s needs before your own
lessons.noon: “Each counting others better than himself” — Lord, right now let me be the first to humble myself.

lessons.title: Only the Self-Emptied Can Be One
lessons.theme: All one in Christ, bound together by love, the bond of perfection

v: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free man, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection.
And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body, and be thankful.

lessons.still: Quietly say, “Lord, I am in you, and they are in you too.” Think of a brother or sister who is very different from you, place the two of you together in the Lord’s embrace, and rest there for a moment.
teach: A pile of planks, each holding on to its own shape, is just a pile of wood. Only when they are willing to be planed, cut to fit and joined together do they become a table. Unity does not mean each plank disappears; it means each finds its place in a greater design. That is the self-emptied life: not ceasing to exist, but entering a greater whole.

Galatians 3:28 says that in Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female; we are all one. The differences remain, but they are no longer dividing walls. Colossians calls love “the bond of perfection,” like a belt that ties all the virtues together. It also says, “let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts.” The word “rule” originally meant “to act as umpire”: when conflict arises, let Christ’s peace make the final call.

This week we have seen Jesus’ prayer for unity (Day 1), how self-rule breeds conflict (Day 2), being eager to keep unity (Day 3) and how humility draws out humility (Day 4). Today it all comes down to one sentence: only the self-emptied can be one. Only when each of us steps down from our own throne can Christ take his seat in our midst. Next week we will see that a united church is a vessel for the coming of the kingdom.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Only through the self-emptied life can we be one and overcome. Self-ruled people have a hundred centres, so they cannot get along; self-emptied people have only one centre: Christ. When we let Jesus reign, we live in one kingdom together; when we let Jesus receive all the glory, we no longer need to fight for ourselves.
q: Who is God? — What does being “all one” in Christ show you about God’s heart?
Who am I? — What invisible wall in your heart still shuts certain people out?
How shall I respond? — In which conflict will you let Christ’s peace be the umpire today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus talked with the Samaritan woman at the well, crossing three high walls at once: race, gender and morality. He did not require her to become a Jew first; he offered her living water first. In him, every dividing wall can be torn down.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, in you we are all one. Tear down the invisible walls in my heart, help me walk in love, and let your peace rule in my heart. I step down from my own throne. Take your seat in our midst, and make us one in heart and mind, to the glory of your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Greet and bless a brother or sister whose background is very different from yours
When opinions differ, first ask for Christ’s peace to rule, then speak
Pray with a spiritual companion for the unity of your church
lessons.noon: “For you are all one in Christ Jesus.” — Lord, right now empty me of self and make me one with all the saints.

mem.t: But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

lessons.title: Your Kingdom Come
lessons.theme: To pray for the kingdom is to ask God to reign in my life

v: Pray like this: “‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”

lessons.still: Slowly say the first three lines of the Lord’s Prayer. Pause at “Let your Kingdom come,” and quietly ask the Lord, “Lord, which corner of my life are you not yet reigning over today?”
teach: A kingdom has three elements: a king, subjects and territory. God’s kingdom is the same: God is the King, believers are his subjects, and the territory is wherever God reigns, from one heart, to one home, to one city. To pray “Your kingdom come” is to ask God to extend his reign to more and more places.

The first words of Jesus’ public ministry were: “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.” To repent is to turn from ruling ourselves to letting God rule. The first three requests of the Lord’s Prayer flow together: hallowing his name, the coming of his kingdom, his will being done on earth as in heaven. In heaven, God’s will is done without hindrance; we ask that it be so on earth too.

This prayer begins with me. I cannot pray “Your kingdom come” while insisting on being king in my own life. The first territory the kingdom claims is my heart. A shift in mindset: God’s kingdom is not only heaven in the future; it is God’s reign beginning in my life today.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Building God’s kingdom system is bringing the Lord’s Prayer to fulfilment. Letting Jesus reign is the heart of the kingdom; letting Jesus receive all the glory is its purpose. All the practices of this year have really been answering one prayer: Your kingdom come.
q: Who is God? — God is King. What does that mean for your life today?
Who am I? — Are you a subject of his kingdom, or still a king in your own little kingdom?
How shall I respond? — Into which corner of your life will you let God’s reign extend today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “If I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you.” The kingdom is not just an idea; it came in concrete form in Jesus: the sick were healed, captives were set free, sinners were forgiven.
lessons.pray: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. Let your kingdom come, and let it come first in my heart. Let your will be done in my home, my work and my relationships as it is in heaven. Reign in every corner of my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Begin and end today with the Lord’s Prayer
Write down one area of your life where you are still “playing king”
Pray for God’s kingdom to come in your city and your nation
lessons.noon: “Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven” — Lord, right now reign in me.

lessons.title: Seek First His Kingdom
lessons.theme: Put the kingdom first, and everything else will find its place

v: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

lessons.still: Name your worries one by one: food, drink, clothing, work, family, the future. After each one, add, “My heavenly Father knows.” Finally, say quietly, “I seek your kingdom first.”
teach: Fill a jar: first the big rocks, then the pebbles, then the sand, and finally the water, and everything fits. Pour in the sand first, and the big rocks will not go in. Life is the same: put in what matters most first, and the rest will find its place. “Seek first his kingdom” is the big rock of life.

Jesus does not say that food, drink and clothing are unimportant. He says, “your heavenly Father knows.” Worry is rooted in thinking everything depends on us. The Gentiles chase after these things because they do not know the Father; God’s children can seek his kingdom and his righteousness first, because the Father takes responsibility for “all these things.” “First” is not only about time; it is about the order of priorities in our hearts.

Seeking the kingdom first is very concrete. With our time: give God the first part of the day. With our money: set aside what is holy first. When making decisions: first ask, “Will this extend God’s kingdom?” In relationships: God first, then ourselves, then people, then tasks. A shift in mindset: from “I’ll look after myself first and then serve God” to “I’ll seek God first, and God will surely look after me.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: The order of relationships (God first, then ourselves, then people, then tasks) is the everyday version of “seek first his kingdom.” It is the order of priorities that lets Jesus reign, and in an anxious age it is the secret of living from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself.
q: Who is God? — “Your heavenly Father knows.” How does this help you face your worries?
Who am I? — What is currently the “big rock” in the jar of your life?
How shall I respond? — Tomorrow, how will you concretely seek his kingdom “first”?
lessons.jesus: At the well Jesus told his disciples, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me, and to accomplish his work.” He could even set aside a meal, because the Father’s kingdom was his most satisfying food. He lived out a life that seeks the kingdom first.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, you know everything I need. I hand my worries over to you and choose to seek your kingdom and your righteousness first. Rearrange the priorities of my life so that you come first, and let everything else find its place in your hands. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Make prayer the first thing you do when you wake tomorrow
Write down one worry, and next to it write, “My heavenly Father knows”
Before making a decision, ask, “Will this extend God’s kingdom?”
lessons.noon: “But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness” — Lord, right now you are my first.

lessons.title: Establishing God’s Domain on Earth
lessons.theme: The kingdom is like yeast, quietly changing the whole from small beginnings

v: He set another parable before them, saying, “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took, and sowed in his field,
which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.”
He spoke another parable to them. “The Kingdom of Heaven is like yeast which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until it was all leavened.”
for God’s Kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

lessons.still: Imagine your home, your office or your small group as a lump of dough, and yourself as a small piece of yeast the Lord has placed in it. Quietly say, “Lord, let your life spread out slowly through me.”
teach: Drop a single drop of ink into a glass of clear water. At first it is just a small dark spot, but soon the whole glass is coloured. The kingdom’s influence does not come through noise or force but through permeation and transformation: quiet yet persistent, small yet real.

The parable of the mustard seed speaks of the kingdom’s expansion: from the smallest of seeds to a tree where birds come to roost. The parable of the yeast speaks of the kingdom’s permeation: hidden in the dough until the whole batch is leavened. Paul explains the kingdom’s essence: it is “not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.” The kingdom is not a building or an organisation; it is the quality of life that God’s reign brings.

Establishing God’s domain on earth means letting righteousness, peace and joy flow out wherever God has placed us: home, workplace, neighbourhood, church. This is the very heart behind the six areas of the life-practice courses: spiritual life, marriage, family, church, work and social life. Each one is kingdom territory. Wherever you are, that is where the kingdom begins.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One purpose: to build God’s kingdom system. God’s kingdom system is not about moving the world into the church, but about bringing God’s reign into every corner of the world. A changed life changes our way of living; a changed way of living changes our relationships; changed relationships change our ministry.
q: Who is God? — God chooses to work in small ways, like a mustard seed and yeast. What does this show you about him?
Who am I? — Are you that piece of yeast where you are?
How shall I respond? — This week, into which area of life will you bring righteousness, peace or joy?
lessons.jesus: Jesus spent thirty-some years on earth, most of them living and working in the small town of Nazareth. He was in no hurry to build a vast organisation. Instead he sowed the seed of the kingdom in villages, in homes and among a small band of disciples, and that seed has now grown into a great tree that fills the earth.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for placing me in my family, my workplace and my community as your yeast. Let your righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit spread out slowly from my life. May your kingdom begin to come right where I am. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Choose one area of your life and write down one kingdom quality you will bring into it
Do one thing at work or at home that promotes justice or peace
Pray specifically for a neighbour or colleague
lessons.noon: “God’s Kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit” — Lord, right now let your kingdom spread out through me.

lessons.title: The Kingdom, the Power and the Glory Are God’s
lessons.theme: The kingdom, the power and the glory all belong to God, not to me

v: Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
For of him and through him and to him are all things. To him be the glory for ever! Amen.

lessons.still: Cup your hands as though you were holding a crown. Think of the power, reputation and achievements you have sought for yourself, and place them all on this crown. Then slowly lift it up and offer it to the Lord who sits on the throne.
teach: At an awards ceremony, a winner steps onto the stage, and his first words are thanks to the teachers and team who trained him. The most moving moment is not when he raises the trophy, but when he turns the honour toward others. In God’s kingdom this is not mere courtesy but the truth: everything belonged to God all along.

The risen Jesus declares, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.” The authority is his, not ours; we only act in his name. After marvelling at God’s wonderful plan of salvation, Paul ends in praise: “For of him, through him, and to him are all things.” From source, through process, to goal, it is all God. That is why the Lord’s Prayer closes with “for yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory.”

The greatest danger in building God’s kingdom system is that, as we go on building, it quietly turns into building “my system.” When ministry bears fruit, numbers grow and our reputation spreads, self-rule creeps back onto the throne. So after every victory we must return to this prayer: yours is the kingdom, yours is the power, yours is the glory.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The two cores: let Jesus reign (the kingdom and the power are his), and let Jesus receive all the glory (the glory is his). Pride is grasping power; humility is laying it down. Giving the kingdom, the power and the glory back to God is humility at its most complete.
q: Who is God? — “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.” What does this show you about the risen Lord?
Who am I? — In your service or achievements, is there glory you have quietly kept for yourself?
How shall I respond? — Which achievement or position of power will you concretely give back to the Lord?
lessons.jesus: When the crowd wanted to make Jesus king by force, he withdrew to the mountain alone. He performed many miracles, yet he said, “I don’t seek my own glory.” He gave all the glory to the Father, and the Father highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, all authority in heaven and on earth is yours; all things are of you, through you and to you. I lay down the power and reputation I have wanted to grasp, and I lay every achievement before your throne. Yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory, for ever. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Look back on one fruit of your service this year, and offer God thanks and glory for it
Publicly honour the work of someone who serves behind the scenes
Each time you finish a task, pray silently, “Glory to you.”
lessons.noon: “To him be the glory for ever!” — Lord, right now all the glory belongs to you.

lessons.title: Ready for the Lord’s Return
lessons.theme: The gospel goes to all the world, and the bride makes herself ready for the Bridegroom

v: This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
He who testifies these things says, “Yes, I am coming soon.” Amen! Yes, come, Lord Jesus!

lessons.still: Quietly say, “Come, Lord Jesus!” Repeat it three times, each time more slowly and more sincerely. Then ask yourself: if the Lord came back today, would my heart be ready?
teach: A bride who knows her bridegroom is coming for her does not stare anxiously at the clock all day. She prepares with joy: getting her things in order, making herself beautiful, letting family and friends know. Expectation brings not fear but hope with a direction.

Jesus said, “This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.” The Lord’s return is closely tied to the spread of the gospel. At the very end of the Bible, the Lord promises, “I come quickly,” and the church answers, “Come, Lord Jesus!” This is the completion of the kingdom prayer: the coming of the kingdom will be fully realised when the King returns.

This week we have moved from Your kingdom come (Day 1), seek first his kingdom (Day 2), establishing God’s domain (Day 3) and glory to God (Day 4) to today’s readiness for the Lord’s return. Next week is the final week of the year. We will look back on this year’s grace and be sent out to become spiritual parents to others, ready for the great revival of the last days.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Building God’s kingdom system is ultimately about preparing the bride to meet the Bridegroom. Multiplication is not about growing the size of the church but about taking the gospel to the whole world. Living in the hope of the Lord’s return means making him King today.
q: Who is God? — What does the promise “I come quickly” show you about this faithful Lord?
Who am I? — Is your attitude to the Lord’s return one of unfamiliarity, fear or longing?
How shall I respond? — Before the Lord returns, who will you share the gospel with?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus ascended, the angels said, “This Jesus, who was received up from you into the sky, will come back in the same way as you saw him going into the sky.” The Lord who died, rose and ascended for us will surely come again. He is the beginning and the end.
lessons.pray: Come, Lord Jesus! Until you return, make me like a bride who is ready, waiting with joy and faithfully proclaiming you. May the good news of the kingdom go out from my lips, and may the people around me be ready to meet you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the name of someone you want to share the gospel with before the Lord returns
End every prayer today with “Come, Lord Jesus”
Share with a spiritual companion what the Lord’s return means for your life today
lessons.noon: “Yes, come” — Lord, right now I make my heart ready to welcome you.

mem.t: He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame and sat down with my Father on his throne.

lessons.title: Looking Back on a Year of Grace
lessons.theme: Raising an Ebenezer: thus far the Lord has helped us

v: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, “The LORD helped us until now.”
Praise the LORD, my soul, and don’t forget all his benefits,

lessons.still: Open your notes from this year or the photo album on your phone, and browse slowly. Each time you see a sign of grace, pause and say, “Lord, thus far you have helped me.” Don’t rush; let thankfulness well up, layer upon layer.
teach: When climbers reach the summit, they often turn around and look back down the way they came: the steep slope, the sheer drop, the place where they almost gave up. Only by looking back do they see how far they have come, and who helped them along the way. Today we stand on the summit of a year, looking back and counting our blessings.

After defeating the Philistines at Mizpah, Samuel set up a stone and named it Ebenezer, meaning “stone of help.” He said, “until now.” This was not an end point but a marker: God helped in the past, and God will surely help in the future. David too commanded his own soul: “Don’t forget all his benefits!” We find it easiest to remember our failures and easiest to forget God’s grace.

This year we have walked through four stages. Rooting (Weeks 1–13): coming home, stillness, Scripture, prayer, humility. Growing (Weeks 14–26): identity, the self-emptied life, the Holy Spirit, self-denial. Fruiting (Weeks 27–39): 920 and the ninefold fruit of the Spirit. Multiplying (Weeks 40–52): 235 relationships, gifts, unity, the kingdom. Each stage is an Ebenezer that God has set up with his own hands.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Changing our mindset changes our life, and changing our life changes our way of living. Looking back over the year is Review carried out in grace: not counting up our own performance, but counting up what God has done. Everything is grace that God has accomplished in Jesus, and the glory goes to him.
q: Who is God? — Looking back over this year, at what moments did God especially show himself as “the God who helps you”?
Who am I? — Of the four stages, in which did you change the most?
How shall I respond? — How will you set up an “Ebenezer” for this year?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus instituted the Lord’s Supper, he said, “Do this in memory of me.” He knew how easily we forget, so he gave us a way to remember. Looking back on grace is remembering the Lord who has walked with us all the way and gave himself for us.
lessons.pray: God who helps me, thus far you have helped me. Thank you for bringing me home this year, and for rooting, growing, fruiting and multiplying in me. My soul, do not forget all his benefits! I offer every step of this year to you; all the glory belongs to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the ten most memorable signs of grace from this year
Choose an object as this year’s “Ebenezer” and put it where you will often see it
Share with a family member or companion one way God helped you this year
lessons.noon: “The LORD helped us until now.” — Lord, right now I remember all your benefits.

lessons.title: The Overcomer’s Promise
lessons.theme: From knocking at the door to sitting on the throne: the overcomer’s path

v: Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with me.
He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame and sat down with my Father on his throne.
I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”

lessons.still: Listen quietly, as if you can hear someone knocking at the door. This year the Lord has knocked at your door again and again. Now open the door of your heart and say to him, “Lord, please come in and eat with me.”
teach: A year ago we began with the prodigal son coming home: the father running to embrace the son returning from a distant land. A year later we read the promise of Revelation: the overcomer will sit with the Lord on his throne. From the doorstep to the throne: that is the whole panorama of the gospel. God not only welcomes us home; he wants us to reign with him.

In Revelation 3:20 the Lord stands at the door and knocks, and he is speaking to the lukewarm church in Laodicea. The Lord had not given up on such a church; if anyone opens the door, he will come in and eat with them. The promise of verse 21 is even more astonishing: the overcomer will sit with the Lord on his throne, “as I also overcame.” Our victory does not depend on ourselves; it is a share in Christ’s victory. He says, “I have overcome the world.”

Overcomers are not people who never fall, but people who open the door again and again to let the Lord in. This year you may have had lukewarm seasons, failures and setbacks, but the Lord is still knocking. The secret of overcoming never changes: let Jesus reign. It is not that I have overcome, but that he overcomes in me.
lessons.light: 321 Light: When the old self’s self-ruled life becomes the new self’s self-emptied life, a defeated life becomes an overcoming life. Humility overcomes pride; the self-emptied life overcomes Satan. The overcomer’s crown is not our own achievement; it is to be laid before the throne, so that Jesus receives all the glory.
q: Who is God? — What kind of Lord knocks at the door and also invites you to sit with him on his throne?
Who am I? — Where this year have you experienced “he overcomes in me”?
How shall I respond? — Which door of your heart still needs to be opened today to let the Lord in?
lessons.jesus: On earth Jesus went through temptation, misunderstanding, betrayal and the cross, and then he said, “I have overcome the world.” His victory was not escaping suffering but passing through it. Having overcome, he sat down on his Father’s throne, and now he invites us to overcome with him.
lessons.pray: Victorious Lord Jesus, thank you for knocking at my door again and again this year. Once more I open the door of my heart and invite you in to reign. I do not overcome by my own strength; I overcome as you overcome in me. One day I will lay my crown at your feet, for you are worthy of all glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down one specific experience this year of overcoming through the Lord
Memorise this week’s verse: Revelation 3:21
Share with someone who is struggling: “The Lord has overcome the world.”
lessons.noon: “He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne” — Lord, right now I open the door and let you reign.

lessons.title: Sent Out: Becoming Spiritual Parents
lessons.theme: Those who have received grace are sent out to multiply life through life

v: But we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother cherishes her own children.
Even so, affectionately longing for you, we were well pleased to impart to you not the Good News of God only, but also our own souls, because you had become very dear to us.
Jesus therefore said to them again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”

lessons.still: First call to mind those who led you to faith and walked with you as you grew, and thank God for them. Then think of one or two people around you who are young in faith, and quietly place their names before the Lord: “Lord, I am willing to walk with them.”
teach: A tree bears fruit, the fruit holds seeds, and the seeds fall to the ground and grow into new trees. The final proof of life is not how tall it grows but whether it can bring forth new life. This year we have been rooted, have grown and have borne fruit in the Lord; now the Lord is sending us out so that life may carry on in others.

Paul told the Thessalonians that he was like a nursing mother caring for her own children, sharing with them not only the gospel but “our own souls.” Elsewhere he says, “Though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers” (1 Corinthians 4:15). Spiritual parents are not speakers on a platform; they are people who walk alongside others, life to life. The risen Lord says, “As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”

Becoming a spiritual parent does not require perfection, only being a few steps further along and being willing to walk alongside. From among your “2,” ask the Lord to show you one or two spiritual children: meet regularly, read the Bible and pray together, share life, walk with them without controlling them. Today you are being sent out, carrying this year’s practices with you, to become a spiritual parent in someone else’s life.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The “3” in 235 means having spiritual parents and becoming one. The final step of the eight steps for changing our mindset is Multiplication. Life first, then relationships, then ministry: not designing a training programme first, but first sharing our life with people. This is the grain of wheat falling into the ground and bearing much fruit.
q: Who is God? — “Even so I send you.” What does this show you about how the Lord sees you?
Who am I? — Do you feel you are “not good enough yet” to be someone’s spiritual parent?
How shall I respond? — For which one or two spiritual children will you pray, and arrange to meet this week?
lessons.jesus: Jesus kept twelve ordinary men close to him, eating with them, walking with them and working with them. What he gave them was not just a curriculum but his own life. In the end he sent them out, and they in turn brought forth generation after generation of spiritual children, all the way down to us today.
lessons.pray: Lord who sends me, thank you for raising me up through many spiritual parents. Now I am willing to be sent by you, to share with others what I have received. Show me the people I should walk alongside, and give me a parent’s heart, like a mother nursing her children, willing to share even my own life with them. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the names of one or two spiritual children you are willing to walk with
This week, take the initiative to meet or call one of them
Thank your spiritual parent, and tell them about your desire to be sent out
lessons.noon: “As the Father has sent me, even so I send you” — Lord, right now I am willing to be sent by you.

lessons.title: Stage Self-Review: Examining the Year
lessons.theme: Examining ourselves under God’s searching gaze, hoping in God’s completing work

v: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts.
See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.

lessons.still: Quietly say, “Search me, God.” Don’t rush to defend yourself, and don’t rush to condemn yourself. Like a patient sitting before a doctor they trust, openly let him examine you, believing it is for your healing.
teach: A health check-up is not meant to frighten us but to catch things early and adjust early. Someone who never has a check-up may seem fine but could be carrying hidden dangers; those who are checked regularly can grow healthier under a doctor’s guidance. The spiritual health self-review is just such an annual check-up.

David asks God, “Search me … try me,” and then asks him to “lead me in the everlasting way.” The goal of self-examination is not to dwell on our faults but to walk the right path. Paul too is confident that he who began a good work in us will complete it. The foundation of self-review is not my performance but God’s faithfulness; not how much I have achieved, but how much more God will complete.

Today, please complete the spiritual health self-review for the fourth stage, and compare it with your results from the first, second and third stages to see the trajectory of the whole year. Which areas have changed? Where does the Lord still need to keep working? Be honest before God, and be hopeful before God. After Review comes Correction, and after Correction comes Repetition: the practice does not end today; it enters a new cycle.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The eight steps for changing our mindset are Information, Revelation, Conviction, Practice, Review, Correction, Repetition and Multiplication. Self-review is the Review step, but we review in grace: our focus is on Jesus, not on our own success or failure. We examine ourselves to respond more deeply to grace, not to earn it.
q: Who is God? — “Will complete it.” How does this help you face your shortcomings?
Who am I? — Comparing your self-reviews across the four stages, what trajectory of growth do you see?
How shall I respond? — In the new year, in which area do you most want to ask the Lord to keep working?
lessons.jesus: The risen Jesus asked Peter three times, “Do you love me?” It was a gentle examination, not to shame him but to restore him. After that examination Jesus said, “Feed my sheep.” The Lord’s searching always comes with a new commission.
lessons.pray: Search me, God, and know my heart; try me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way. Thank you that he who began a good work in me will complete it. I entrust this year to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Complete this stage's spiritual health self-review
Compare your self-reviews across the four stages, and write down three areas of growth and one need
Share what you discovered in your self-review with a spiritual companion or spiritual parent
lessons.noon: “Search me, God, and know my heart” — Lord, right now I stand open before you.

lessons.title: Let Jesus Reign in the New Year
lessons.theme: Heading toward the great revival of the last days, letting Jesus reign in the new year

v: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.
that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, those on earth, and those under the earth,
and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

lessons.still: Stand up, open your hands, and offer the new year to the Lord, saying, “Lord Jesus, in the new year you are King.” Then wait quietly, asking the Holy Spirit to pour out on you and on those you love.
teach: One spark lights a torch; one torch lights ten; ten light a hundred. A city at night is not lit by one huge lamp but by thousands upon thousands of small lights shining together. The great revival of the last days likewise begins with lives that are set alight, one by one, and go on to set others alight.

Joel prophesied, “I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh.” On the day of Pentecost, Peter declared that this prophecy had begun to be fulfilled. From that day on, the outpouring of the Spirit has spread from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth, and will do so until the Lord returns. Philippians pictures the end: everything in heaven, on earth and under the earth will bow the knee at the name of Jesus, and every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. That is where revival is ultimately heading.

This year began with the prodigal coming home and ends today with being sent out. Humility is the key to revival: revival does not begin with large gatherings but with one heart willing to let Jesus reign. In the new year, may the Lord make you a lamp that has been set alight, carrying your 235 relationships into your family, workplace, church and society, building God’s kingdom system and welcoming the Lord’s return.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Three foundations, two cores, one purpose. Jesus is my example; Scripture is my standard; the Holy Spirit is my guide. Let Jesus reign; let Jesus receive all the glory. Build what belongs to God. In the new year, let 321 become the rhythm of your life, until every tongue confesses that Jesus is Lord.
q: Who is God? — What is the heart of the God who promises to pour out his Spirit on all flesh toward the last generation?
Who am I? — Are you willing to be a torch in the revival of the last days?
How shall I respond? — In the new year, in what concrete way will you let Jesus reign every day?
lessons.jesus: Before his ascension Jesus promised, “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you.” He ascended to the Father’s right hand, poured out the Spirit, and is still extending his kingdom today. He is both the source and the goal of revival: every knee will bow to him.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, in the new year I give the throne to you. Pour out your Spirit on me, my family, my church and my city, and make me a lamp that is set alight and that sets others alight. May every knee bow to you and every tongue confess that you are Lord. Come, Lord Jesus! In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write a “Let Jesus Reign” declaration for the new year, then sign and date it
Pray with one heart with a fellow soldier for the great revival of the last days
Plan your quiet times and your times of walking with others for the first week of the new year
lessons.noon: “I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh” — Lord, right now set me alight; in the new year you are King.
